<h1 id="superset-annotation-layers">Annotation Layers</h1>

## Get a list of annotation layers

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/api/v1/annotation_layer/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v1/annotation_layer/`

Gets a list of annotation layers, use Rison or JSON query parameters for filtering, sorting, pagination and for selecting specific columns and metadata.

<h3 id="get-a-list-of-annotation-layers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|q|query|[get_list_schema](#schemaget_list_schema)|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": 0,
  "description_columns": {
    "column_name": "A Nice description for the column"
  },
  "ids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "label_columns": {
    "column_name": "A Nice label for the column"
  },
  "list_columns": [
    "string"
  ],
  "list_title": "List Items",
  "order_columns": [
    "string"
  ],
  "result": [
    {
      "changed_by": {
        "first_name": "string",
        "last_name": "string"
      },
      "changed_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "changed_on_delta_humanized": null,
      "created_by": {
        "first_name": "string",
        "last_name": "string"
      },
      "created_on": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "descr": "string",
      "id": 0,
      "name": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string"
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

## Import multiple assets

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/api/v1/assets/import/ \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'bundle=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'encrypted_extra_secrets=string' \
  -F 'overwrite=true' \
  -F 'passwords=string' \
  -F 'sparse=true' \
  -F 'ssh_tunnel_passwords=string' \
  -F 'ssh_tunnel_private_key_passwords=string' \
  -F 'ssh_tunnel_private_keys=string'
```

`POST /api/v1/assets/import/`

> Body parameter

```yaml
bundle: string
encrypted_extra_secrets: string
overwrite: true
passwords: string
sparse: true
ssh_tunnel_passwords: string
ssh_tunnel_private_key_passwords: string
ssh_tunnel_private_keys: string
```

<h3 id="import-multiple-assets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» bundle|body|string(binary)|false|upload file (ZIP or JSON)|
|» encrypted_extra_secrets|body|string|false|JSON map of secret values for masked encrypted_extra fields. Each key is a database file path and the value is a map of JSONPath expressions to secret values. For example: `{"databases/db.yaml": {"$.credentials_info.secret": "foo"}}`.|
|» overwrite|body|boolean|false|overwrite existing assets? Defaults to ``true`` for backwards compatibility. When ``false``, the import fails if any of the assets already exist.|
|» passwords|body|string|false|JSON map of passwords for each featured database in the ZIP file. If the ZIP includes a database config in the path `databases/MyDatabase.yaml`, the password should be provided in the following format: `{"databases/MyDatabase.yaml": "my_password"}`.|
|» sparse|body|boolean|false|allow sparse update of resources|
|» ssh_tunnel_passwords|body|string|false|JSON map of passwords for each ssh_tunnel associated to a featured database in the ZIP file. If the ZIP includes a ssh_tunnel config in the path `databases/MyDatabase.yaml`, the password should be provided in the following format: `{"databases/MyDatabase.yaml": "my_password"}`.|
|» ssh_tunnel_private_key_passwords|body|string|false|JSON map of private_key_passwords for each ssh_tunnel associated to a featured database in the ZIP file. If the ZIP includes a ssh_tunnel config in the path `databases/MyDatabase.yaml`, the private_key should be provided in the following format: `{"databases/MyDatabase.yaml": "my_private_key_password"}`.|
|» ssh_tunnel_private_keys|body|string|false|JSON map of private_keys for each ssh_tunnel associated to a featured database in the ZIP file. If the ZIP includes a ssh_tunnel config in the path `databases/MyDatabase.yaml`, the private_key should be provided in the following format: `{"databases/MyDatabase.yaml": "my_private_key"}`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string"
}
```

## Invalidate cache records and remove the database records

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/api/v1/cachekey/invalidate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "datasource_uids": [
      "string"
    ],
    "datasources": [
      {
        "catalog": "string",
        "database_name": "string",
        "datasource_name": "string",
        "datasource_type": "table",
        "schema": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/cachekey/invalidate`

Takes a list of datasources, finds and invalidates the associated cache records and removes the database records.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "datasource_uids": [
    "string"
  ],
  "datasources": [
    {
      "catalog": "string",
      "database_name": "string",
      "datasource_name": "string",
      "datasource_type": "table",
      "schema": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CacheInvalidationRequestSchema](#schemacacheinvalidationrequestschema)|true|A list of datasources uuid or the tuples of database and datasource names|
|» datasource_uids|body|[string]|false|The uid of the dataset/datasource this new chart will use. A complete datasource identification needs `datasource_uid` |
|» datasources|body|[[Datasource](#schemadatasource)]|false|A list of the data source and database names|

|» datasource_type|body|string|true|The type of dataset/datasource identified on `datasource_id`.|

|» editors|body|[integer \| object]|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|Subject ID, not a user ID.|

|» » id|body|integer|true|none|

|» external_url|body|string \| null|false|none|

|» params|body|string \| null|false|Parameters are generated dynamically when clicking the save or overwrite button in the explore view. This JSON object for power users who may want to alter specific parameters.|
|» query_context|body|string \| null|false|The query context represents the queries that need to run in order to generate the data the visualization, and in what format the data should be returned.|
|» query_context_generation|body|boolean \| null|false|The query context generation represents whether the query_contextis user generated or not so that it does not update user modifiedstate.|
|» slice_name|body|string|true|The name of the chart.|
|» uuid|body|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|

|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|

|» » type|body|string|true|none|
|» viz_type|body|string|false|The type of chart visualization used.|

<h3 id="return-payload-data-response-for-the-given-query-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ChartDataQueryContextSchema](#schemachartdataquerycontextschema)|true|A query context consists of a datasource from which to fetch data and one or many query objects.|
|» async_mode|body|boolean \| null|false|Opt this request into asynchronous execution on the Global Task Framework (requires the GLOBAL_ASYNC_QUERIES feature flag). When true the response is HTTP 202 with the query task ids to poll; when absent or false the query runs synchronously (HTTP 200). Default: `false`.|
|» custom_cache_timeout|body|integer \| null|false|Override the default cache timeout|
|» datasource|body|[ChartDataDatasource](#schemachartdatadatasource)|false|none|
|» force|body|boolean \| null|false|Should the queries be forced to load from the source. Default: `false`|
|» force_nonce|body|string \| null|false|Forced-refresh idempotency token for a single-query request: the async task's UUID (as returned in the 202 `task_ids`). Sent on the synchronous read-back of a forced refresh so it reads the result the task warmed instead of recomputing; concurrent refreshes joining the same shared task read back under the same token. Multi-query requests set the per-query `force_nonce` on each query instead. Ignored when `force` is false.|
|» form_data|body|object \| null|false|none|
|» queries|body|[[ChartDataQueryObject](#schemachartdataqueryobject)]|false|none|
|» result_format|body|string|false|none|
|» result_type|body|string|false|none|
|» tab_id|body|string \| null|false|Opaque per-browser-tab id (see the frontend `getTabId`). On an async request it ref-counts this tab as a consumer of the shared chart-data task so a cancel/navigate-away from one tab doesn't abort a task another tab still awaits. Read by the API as a request-level routing hint; not part of the query context.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» result_format|csv|
|» result_format|json|
|» result_format|xlsx|
|» result_format|arrow|
|» result_type|columns|
|» result_type|full|
|» result_type|query|
|» result_type|results|
|» result_type|samples|
|» result_type|timegrains|
|» result_type|post_processed|
|» result_type|drill_detail|

## Import chart(s) with associated datasets and databases

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/api/v1/chart/import/ \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'formData=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'overwrite=true' \
  -F 'passwords=string' \
  -F 'ssh_tunnel_passwords=string' \
  -F 'ssh_tunnel_private_key_passwords=string' \
  -F 'ssh_tunnel_private_keys=string'
```

`POST /api/v1/chart/import/`

> Body parameter

```yaml
formData: string
overwrite: true
passwords: string
ssh_tunnel_passwords: string
ssh_tunnel_private_key_passwords: string
ssh_tunnel_private_keys: string
```

<h3 id="import-charts-with-associated-datasets-and-databases-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» formData|body|string(binary)|false|upload file (ZIP)|
|» overwrite|body|boolean|false|overwrite existing charts?|
|» passwords|body|string|false|JSON map of passwords for each featured database in the ZIP file. If the ZIP includes a database config in the path `databases/MyDatabase.yaml`, the password should be provided in the following format: `{"databases/MyDatabase.yaml": "my_password"}`.|
|» ssh_tunnel_passwords|body|string|false|JSON map of passwords for each ssh_tunnel associated to a featured database in the ZIP file. If the ZIP includes a ssh_tunnel config in the path `databases/MyDatabase.yaml`, the password should be provided in the following format: `{"databases/MyDatabase.yaml": "my_password"}`.|
|» ssh_tunnel_private_key_passwords|body|string|false|JSON map of private_key_passwords for each ssh_tunnel associated to a featured database in the ZIP file. If the ZIP includes a ssh_tunnel config in the path `databases/MyDatabase.yaml`, the private_key should be provided in the following format: `{"databases/MyDatabase.yaml": "my_private_key_password"}`.|
|» ssh_tunnel_private_keys|body|string|false|JSON map of private_keys for each ssh_tunnel associated to a featured database in the ZIP file. If the ZIP includes a ssh_tunnel config in the path `databases/MyDatabase.yaml`, the private_key should be provided in the following format: `{"databases/MyDatabase.yaml": "my_private_key"}`.|

`PUT /api/v1/chart/warm_up_cache`

Warms up the cache for the chart. Note for slices a force refresh occurs. In terms of the `extra_filters` these can be obtained from records in the JSON encoded `logs.json` column associated with the `explore` action.

## Return payload data response for a chart

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/api/v1/chart/0/data/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v1/chart/{pk}/data/`

Takes a chart ID and uses the query context stored when the chart was saved to return payload data response. When filters_dashboard_id is provided, the chart's compiled SQL includes in scope dashboard filter default values.

<h3 id="return-payload-data-response-for-a-chart-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pk|path|integer|true|The chart ID|
|format|query|string|false|The format in which the data should be returned|
|type|query|string|false|The type in which the data should be returned|
|force|query|boolean|false|Should the queries be forced to load from the source|
|filters_dashboard_id|query|integer|false|Dashboard ID whose filter defaults should be applied to the chart's query context. The chart must belong to the specified dashboard. Only in scope filters with static default values are applied; filters that require a database query (I.E. defaultToFirstItem) or have no default are reported in the dashboard_filters response metadata.|

## Get the sub-layer charts declared by a deck.gl Multiple Layers chart

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/api/v1/chart/0/deck_layers/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v1/chart/{pk}/deck_layers/`

Multiple Layers charts (viz_type "deck_multi") reference other saved charts as layers via their `deck_slices` config, but those layer charts typically sit on no dashboard of their own, so a per-layer `GET /api/v1/chart/<id>` can 404 for a principal (e.g. an embedded guest) who is only entitled to the container. This endpoint gates on the container chart and resolves the layers it declares, mirroring the access the legacy explore_json pipeline granted server-side.

<h3 id="get-the-sub-layer-charts-declared-by-a-deckgl-multiple-layers-chart-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|pk|path|integer|true|The id of the Multiple Layers container chart|

```json
    {
      "datasource_id": 0,
      "datasource_type": "string",
      "params": "string",

    }
  ]
}
```

## Download a completed dashboard Excel export

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/api/v1/dashboard/export_xlsx/download/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/
```

`GET /api/v1/dashboard/export_xlsx/download/{job_id}/`

Intentionally requires no login: the unguessable job_id, emailed only to the original requester (or handed to their own session via export_xlsx_status), is the credential. The dashboard access check already ran once, when the export was requested -- see security_manager.raise_for_access in export_xlsx. The file streams through Superset with the deployment's own storage credentials instead of redirecting to a signed storage URL, so it works for ambient identities that cannot sign (e.g. workload identity federation) and never mints a bearer URL Superset cannot observe or revoke.

<h3 id="download-a-completed-dashboard-excel-export-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|job_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The job_id from the export_xlsx response|

<h3 id="download-a-completed-dashboard-excel-export-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The .xlsx file as an attachment|None|
|410|Gone|The link is unknown, expired, or the export failed|None|
|501|Not Implemented|Excel export is not configured on this server|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Poll the status of a dashboard Excel export job

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/api/v1/dashboard/export_xlsx/status/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v1/dashboard/export_xlsx/status/{job_id}/`

For a session with no email address to be notified at (e.g. an embedded/guest session), the frontend polls this endpoint with the job_id from the export_xlsx response instead of waiting for an email. Behind the same @protect() as the export request itself, unlike the login-free download_xlsx stream (which also has to work when clicked from a plain email link, possibly with no active session at all).

<h3 id="poll-the-status-of-a-dashboard-excel-export-job-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|job_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The job_id from the export_xlsx response|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string"
}
```

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Job status: {"status": "pending"} while queued, {"status": "running"} once a worker has started executing, {"status": "ready", "download_url": "..."} once the file is available, or {"status": "error", "message": "..."} if the export failed.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|Inline|

<h3 id="import-dashboards-with-associated-chartsdatasetsdatabases-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|» overwrite_all|body|boolean|false|overwrite all existing assets within the dashboard?|
|» passwords|body|string|false|JSON map of passwords for each featured database in the ZIP file. If the ZIP includes a database config in the path `databases/MyDatabase.yaml`, the password should be provided in the following format: `{"databases/MyDatabase.yaml": "my_password"}`.|
|» ssh_tunnel_passwords|body|string|false|JSON map of passwords for each ssh_tunnel associated to a featured database in the ZIP file. If the ZIP includes a ssh_tunnel config in the path `databases/MyDatabase.yaml`, the password should be provided in the following format: `{"databases/MyDatabase.yaml": "my_password"}`.|
|» ssh_tunnel_private_key_passwords|body|string|false|JSON map of private_key_passwords for each ssh_tunnel associated to a featured database in the ZIP file. If the ZIP includes a ssh_tunnel config in the path `databases/MyDatabase.yaml`, the private_key should be provided in the following format: `{"databases/MyDatabase.yaml": "my_private_key_password"}`.|
|» ssh_tunnel_private_keys|body|string|false|JSON map of private_keys for each ssh_tunnel associated to a featured database in the ZIP file. If the ZIP includes a ssh_tunnel config in the path `databases/MyDatabase.yaml`, the private_key should be provided in the following format: `{"databases/MyDatabase.yaml": "my_private_key"}`.|

## Create a copy of an existing dashboard

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/api/v1/dashboard/string/copy/ \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "css": "string",
    "dashboard_title": "string",
    "duplicate_slices": true,
    "json_metadata": "string",
    "replace_metadata": false
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/dashboard/{id_or_slug}/copy/`

Settings merge with the source by default. Set replace_metadata to true to use json_metadata as complete settings, as for a version fork. Chart-specific settings are pruned and remapped in both modes.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "css": "string",
  "dashboard_title": "string",
  "duplicate_slices": true,
  "json_metadata": "string",
  "replace_metadata": false
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-copy-of-an-existing-dashboard-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id_or_slug|path|string|true|The dashboard id or slug|
|body|body|[DashboardCopySchema](#schemadashboardcopyschema)|true|none|
|» css|body|string|false|Override CSS for the dashboard.|
|» dashboard_title|body|string \| null|false|A title for the dashboard.|
|» duplicate_slices|body|boolean|false|Whether or not to also copy all charts on the dashboard|
|» json_metadata|body|string|true|This JSON object is generated dynamically when clicking the save or overwrite button in the dashboard view. It is exposed here for reference and for power users who may want to alter  specific parameters.|
|» replace_metadata|body|boolean|false|Use json_metadata as the complete copy settings instead of merging with the source dashboard's settings. Defaults to false. Chart-specific settings are pruned and remapped in both modes.|

> Example responses

```json
}
```

## Export dashboard chart data to Excel

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/api/v1/dashboard/0/export_xlsx/ \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "active_data_mask": {
      "property1": {},
      "property2": {}
    },
    "mode": "data"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/dashboard/{pk}/export_xlsx/`

Writes each chart to a worksheet. With export storage configured, the work is queued: the requesting user is emailed a download link when they have an address on file, and either way the returned job id can be polled at export_xlsx/status/<job_id>/ for status and, once ready, the download link. Without export storage, eligible data workbooks are returned in the response.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "active_data_mask": {
    "property1": {},
    "property2": {}
  },
  "mode": "data"
}
```

<h3 id="export-dashboard-chart-data-to-excel-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pk|path|integer|true|The dashboard id|
|body|body|[DashboardExportXlsxPostSchema](#schemadashboardexportxlsxpostschema)|false|none|
|» active_data_mask|body|object|false|Live dashboard filter state keyed by native filter id, each carrying an extraFormData object.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» mode|body|string|false|Export mode: 'data' streams each chart's tabular result (default); 'images' embeds non-table charts as rendered images and keeps table charts tabular.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» mode|data|
|» mode|images|

## Create a new dashboard's permanent link

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/api/v1/dashboard/string/permalink \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "dataMask": {
      "extraFormData": {
        "filters": [
          {
            "col": "tz_offset",
            "op": ">=",
            "val": [
              1000
            ]
          },
          {
            "col": "tz_offset",
            "op": "<=",
            "val": [
              2000
            ]
          }
        ]
      },
      "filterState": {
        "label": "1000 <= x <= 200",
        "value": [
          1000,
          2000
        ]
      },
      "id": "NATIVE_FILTER_ID"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/dashboard/{pk}/permalink`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "dataMask": {
    "extraFormData": {
      "filters": [

            1000
          ]
        },
        {
          "col": "tz_offset",
          "op": "<=",
          "val": [
            2000
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    "filterState": {
      "label": "1000 <= x <= 200",
      "value": [
        1000,
        2000
      ]
    },
    "id": "NATIVE_FILTER_ID"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-database-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[DatabaseRestApi.post](#schemadatabaserestapi.post)|true|Database schema|
|» allow_ctas|body|boolean|false|Allow CREATE TABLE AS option in SQL Lab|
|» allow_cvas|body|boolean|false|Allow CREATE VIEW AS option in SQL Lab|
|» allow_dml|body|boolean|false|Allow users to run non-SELECT statements (UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE, ...) in SQL Lab|
|» allow_file_upload|body|boolean|false|Allow to upload CSV file data into this databaseIf selected, please set the schemas allowed for csv upload in Extra.|
|» allow_run_async|body|boolean|false|Operate the database in asynchronous mode, meaning that the queries are executed on remote workers as opposed to on the web server itself. This assumes that you have a Celery worker setup as well as a results backend. Refer to the installation docs for more information.|
|» cache_timeout|body|integer \| null|false|Duration (in seconds) of the caching timeout for charts of this database. A timeout of 0 indicates that the cache never expires, and -1 bypasses the cache. Note this defaults to the global timeout if undefined.|
|» configuration_method|body|string|false|Configuration_method is used on the frontend to inform the backend whether to explode parameters or to provide only a sqlalchemy_uri.|
|» database_name|body|string|true|A database name to identify this connection.|
|» driver|body|string \| null|false|SQLAlchemy driver to use|
|» engine|body|string \| null|false|SQLAlchemy engine to use|
|» expose_in_sqllab|body|boolean|false|Expose this database to SQLLab|
|» external_url|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» extra|body|string|false|<p>JSON string containing extra configuration elements.<br>1. The <code>engine_params</code> object gets unpacked into the <a href="https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/core/engines.html#sqlalchemy.create_engine" rel="noopener noreferrer">sqlalchemy.create_engine</a> call, while the <code>metadata_params</code> gets unpacked into the <a href="https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/rel_1_0/core/metadata.html#sqlalchemy.schema.MetaData" rel="noopener noreferrer">sqlalchemy.MetaData</a> call.<br>2. The <code>metadata_cache_timeout</code> is a cache timeout setting in seconds for metadata fetch of this database. Specify it as <strong>"metadata_cache_timeout": {"schema_cache_timeout": 600, "table_cache_timeout": 600}</strong>. If unset, cache will not be enabled for the functionality. A timeout of 0 indicates that the cache never expires.<br>3. The <code>schemas_allowed_for_file_upload</code> is a comma separated list of schemas that CSVs are allowed to upload to. Specify it as <strong>"schemas_allowed_for_file_upload": ["public", "csv_upload"]</strong>. If database flavor does not support schema or any schema is allowed to be accessed, just leave the list empty<br>4. The <code>version</code> field is a string specifying the this db's version. This should be used with Presto DBs so that the syntax is correct<br>5. The <code>allows_virtual_table_explore</code> field is a boolean specifying whether or not the Explore button in SQL Lab results is shown.<br>6. The <code>disable_data_preview</code> field is a boolean specifying whether or not data preview queries will be run when fetching table metadata in SQL Lab.<br>7. The <code>disable_drill_to_detail</code> field is a boolean specifying whether or not drill to detail is disabled for the database.<br>8. The <code>allow_multi_catalog</code> indicates if the database allows changing the default catalog when running queries and creating datasets.<br>9. The <code>disable_sampling_read_limit_override</code> field is a boolean specifying whether system-generated sampling queries (filter values, samples/preview, datetime format detection) that an engine rejects with a read-limit error should fail outright instead of being retried once with the engine's bounded-read override. Only affects engines that implement such an override.</p>|
|» force_ctas_schema|body|string \| null|false|When allowing CREATE TABLE AS option in SQL Lab, this option forces the table to be created in this schema|
|» impersonate_user|body|boolean|false|If Presto, all the queries in SQL Lab are going to be executed as the currently logged on user who must have permission to run them.<br/>If Hive and hive.server2.enable.doAs is enabled, will run the queries as service account, but impersonate the currently logged on user via hive.server2.proxy.user property.|
|» is_managed_externally|body|boolean \| null|false|none|
|» masked_encrypted_extra|body|string \| null|false|<p>JSON string containing additional connection configuration.<br>This is used to provide connection information for systems like Hive, Presto, and BigQuery, which do not conform to the username:password syntax normally used by SQLAlchemy.</p>|
|» parameters|body|object|false|DB-specific parameters for configuration|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» server_cert|body|string \| null|false|<p>Optional CA_BUNDLE contents to validate HTTPS requests. Only available on certain database engines.</p>|
|» sqlalchemy_uri|body|string|false|<p>Refer to the <a href="https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/rel_1_2/core/engines.html#database-urls" rel="noopener noreferrer">SqlAlchemy docs</a> for more information on how to structure your URI.</p>|
|» ssh_tunnel|body|object \| null|false|none|
|» » id|body|integer \| null|false|SSH Tunnel ID (for updates)|
|» » password|body|string|false|none|
|» » private_key|body|string|false|none|
|» » private_key_password|body|string|false|none|
|» » server_address|body|string|false|none|
|» » server_host_key|body|string \| null|false|Expected SSH server host key in authorized-key form (e.g. 'ssh-ed25519 AAAA...'). When set, the server's host key is verified against it before the tunnel is opened.|
|» » server_port|body|integer|false|none|
|» » username|body|string|false|none|
|» uuid|body|string|false|none|

## Import database(s) with associated datasets

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/api/v1/database/import/ \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'encrypted_extra_secrets=string' \
  -F 'formData=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'overwrite=true' \
  -F 'passwords=string' \
  -F 'ssh_tunnel_passwords=string' \
  -F 'ssh_tunnel_private_key_passwords=string' \
  -F 'ssh_tunnel_private_keys=string'
```

`POST /api/v1/database/import/`

> Body parameter

```yaml
encrypted_extra_secrets: string
formData: string
overwrite: true
passwords: string
ssh_tunnel_passwords: string
ssh_tunnel_private_key_passwords: string
ssh_tunnel_private_keys: string
```

<h3 id="import-databases-with-associated-datasets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» encrypted_extra_secrets|body|string|false|JSON map of sensitive values for masked_encrypted_extra fields. Keys are file paths (e.g., "databases/db.yaml") and values are JSON objects mapping JSONPath expressions to secrets. (e.g., `{"databases/MyDatabase.yaml": {"$.credentials_info.private_key": "actual_key"}}`).|
|» formData|body|string(binary)|false|upload file (ZIP)|
|» overwrite|body|boolean|false|overwrite existing databases?|
|» passwords|body|string|false|JSON map of passwords for each featured database in the ZIP file. If the ZIP includes a database config in the path `databases/MyDatabase.yaml`, the password should be provided in the following format: `{"databases/MyDatabase.yaml": "my_password"}`.|
|» ssh_tunnel_passwords|body|string|false|JSON map of passwords for each ssh_tunnel associated to a featured database in the ZIP file. If the ZIP includes a ssh_tunnel config in the path `databases/MyDatabase.yaml`, the password should be provided in the following format: `{"databases/MyDatabase.yaml": "my_password"}`.|
|» ssh_tunnel_private_key_passwords|body|string|false|JSON map of private_key_passwords for each ssh_tunnel associated to a featured database in the ZIP file. If the ZIP includes a ssh_tunnel config in the path `databases/MyDatabase.yaml`, the private_key should be provided in the following format: `{"databases/MyDatabase.yaml": "my_private_key_password"}`.|
|» ssh_tunnel_private_keys|body|string|false|JSON map of private_keys for each ssh_tunnel associated to a featured database in the ZIP file. If the ZIP includes a ssh_tunnel config in the path `databases/MyDatabase.yaml`, the private_key should be provided in the following format: `{"databases/MyDatabase.yaml": "my_private_key"}`.|

## Test a database connection

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/api/v1/database/test_connection/ \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "configuration_method": "sqlalchemy_form",
    "database_name": "string",
    "driver": "string",
    "engine": "string",
    "extra": "string",
    "impersonate_user": true,
    "masked_encrypted_extra": "string",
    "parameters": {
      "property1": null,
      "property2": null
    },
    "server_cert": "string",
    "sqlalchemy_uri": "string",
    "ssh_tunnel": {
      "id": 0,
      "password": "string",
      "private_key": "string",
      "private_key_password": "string",
      "server_address": "string",
      "server_host_key": "string",
      "server_port": 0,
      "username": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/database/test_connection/`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "configuration_method": "sqlalchemy_form",
  "database_name": "string",
  "driver": "string",
  "engine": "string",
  "extra": "string",
  "impersonate_user": true,
  "masked_encrypted_extra": "string",
  "parameters": {
    "property1": null,
    "property2": null
  },
  "server_cert": "string",
  "sqlalchemy_uri": "string",
  "ssh_tunnel": {
    "id": 0,
    "password": "string",
    "private_key": "string",
    "private_key_password": "string",
    "server_address": "string",
    "server_host_key": "string",
    "server_port": 0,
    "username": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="test-a-database-connection-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[DatabaseTestConnectionSchema](#schemadatabasetestconnectionschema)|true|Database schema|
|» configuration_method|body|string|false|Configuration_method is used on the frontend to inform the backend whether to explode parameters or to provide only a sqlalchemy_uri.|
|» database_name|body|string \| null|false|A database name to identify this connection.|
|» driver|body|string \| null|false|SQLAlchemy driver to use|
|» engine|body|string \| null|false|SQLAlchemy engine to use|
|» extra|body|string|false|<p>JSON string containing extra configuration elements.<br>1. The <code>engine_params</code> object gets unpacked into the <a href="https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/core/engines.html#sqlalchemy.create_engine" rel="noopener noreferrer">sqlalchemy.create_engine</a> call, while the <code>metadata_params</code> gets unpacked into the <a href="https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/rel_1_0/core/metadata.html#sqlalchemy.schema.MetaData" rel="noopener noreferrer">sqlalchemy.MetaData</a> call.<br>2. The <code>metadata_cache_timeout</code> is a cache timeout setting in seconds for metadata fetch of this database. Specify it as <strong>"metadata_cache_timeout": {"schema_cache_timeout": 600, "table_cache_timeout": 600}</strong>. If unset, cache will not be enabled for the functionality. A timeout of 0 indicates that the cache never expires.<br>3. The <code>schemas_allowed_for_file_upload</code> is a comma separated list of schemas that CSVs are allowed to upload to. Specify it as <strong>"schemas_allowed_for_file_upload": ["public", "csv_upload"]</strong>. If database flavor does not support schema or any schema is allowed to be accessed, just leave the list empty<br>4. The <code>version</code> field is a string specifying the this db's version. This should be used with Presto DBs so that the syntax is correct<br>5. The <code>allows_virtual_table_explore</code> field is a boolean specifying whether or not the Explore button in SQL Lab results is shown.<br>6. The <code>disable_data_preview</code> field is a boolean specifying whether or not data preview queries will be run when fetching table metadata in SQL Lab.<br>7. The <code>disable_drill_to_detail</code> field is a boolean specifying whether or not drill to detail is disabled for the database.<br>8. The <code>allow_multi_catalog</code> indicates if the database allows changing the default catalog when running queries and creating datasets.<br>9. The <code>disable_sampling_read_limit_override</code> field is a boolean specifying whether system-generated sampling queries (filter values, samples/preview, datetime format detection) that an engine rejects with a read-limit error should fail outright instead of being retried once with the engine's bounded-read override. Only affects engines that implement such an override.</p>|
|» impersonate_user|body|boolean|false|If Presto, all the queries in SQL Lab are going to be executed as the currently logged on user who must have permission to run them.<br/>If Hive and hive.server2.enable.doAs is enabled, will run the queries as service account, but impersonate the currently logged on user via hive.server2.proxy.user property.|
|» masked_encrypted_extra|body|string \| null|false|<p>JSON string containing additional connection configuration.<br>This is used to provide connection information for systems like Hive, Presto, and BigQuery, which do not conform to the username:password syntax normally used by SQLAlchemy.</p>|
|» parameters|body|object|false|DB-specific parameters for configuration|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» server_cert|body|string \| null|false|<p>Optional CA_BUNDLE contents to validate HTTPS requests. Only available on certain database engines.</p>|
|» sqlalchemy_uri|body|string|false|<p>Refer to the <a href="https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/rel_1_2/core/engines.html#database-urls" rel="noopener noreferrer">SqlAlchemy docs</a> for more information on how to structure your URI.</p>|
|» ssh_tunnel|body|object \| null|false|none|
|» » id|body|integer \| null|false|SSH Tunnel ID (for updates)|
|» » password|body|string|false|none|
|» » private_key|body|string|false|none|
|» » private_key_password|body|string|false|none|
|» » server_address|body|string|false|none|
|» » server_host_key|body|string \| null|false|Expected SSH server host key in authorized-key form (e.g. 'ssh-ed25519 AAAA...'). When set, the server's host key is verified against it before the tunnel is opened.|
|» » server_port|body|integer|false|none|
|» » username|body|string|false|none|

## Upload a file to a database table

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/api/v1/database/0/upload/ \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'already_exists=fail' \
  -F 'column_data_types=string' \
  -F 'column_dates=["string"]' \
  -F 'columns_read=["string"]' \
  -F 'dataframe_index=true' \
  -F 'day_first=true' \
  -F 'decimal_character=string' \
  -F 'delimiter=string' \
  -F 'file=string' \
  -F 'header_row=0' \
  -F 'index_column=string' \
  -F 'index_label=string' \
  -F 'null_values=["string"]' \
  -F 'rows_to_read=1' \
  -F 'schema=string' \
  -F 'sheet_name=string' \
  -F 'skip_blank_lines=true' \
  -F 'skip_initial_space=true' \
  -F 'skip_rows=0' \
  -F 'table_name=string' \
  -F 'type=csv'
```

`POST /api/v1/database/{pk}/upload/`

> Body parameter

```yaml
already_exists: fail
column_data_types: string
column_dates:
  - string
columns_read:
  - string
dataframe_index: true
day_first: true
decimal_character: string
delimiter: string
file: string
header_row: 0
index_column: string
index_label: string
null_values:
  - string
rows_to_read: 1
schema: string
sheet_name: string
skip_blank_lines: true
skip_initial_space: true
skip_rows: 0
table_name: string
type: csv
```

<h3 id="upload-a-file-to-a-database-table-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pk|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|[UploadPostSchema](#schemauploadpostschema)|true|none|
|» already_exists|body|string|false|What to do if the table already exists accepts: fail, replace, append|
|» column_data_types|body|string|false|[CSV only] A dictionary with column names and their data types if you need to change the defaults. Example: {'user_id':'int'}. Check Python Pandas library for supported data types|
|» column_dates|body|[string]|false|[CSV and Excel only] A list of column names that should be parsed as dates. Example: date,timestamp|
|» columns_read|body|[string]|false|A List of the column names that should be read|
|» dataframe_index|body|boolean|false|Write dataframe index as a column.|
|» day_first|body|boolean|false|[CSV only] DD/MM format dates, international and European format|
|» decimal_character|body|string|false|[CSV and Excel only] Character to recognize as decimal point. Default is '.'|
|» delimiter|body|string|false|[CSV only] The character used to separate values in the CSV file (e.g., a comma, semicolon, or tab).|
|» file|body|string(text/csv)|true|The file to upload|
|» header_row|body|integer|false|[CSV and Excel only] Row containing the headers to use as column names (0 is first line of data). Leave empty if there is no header row.|
|» index_column|body|string|false|[CSV and Excel only] Column to use as the row labels of the dataframe. Leave empty if no index column|
|» index_label|body|string|false|Index label for index column.|
|» null_values|body|[string]|false|[CSV and Excel only] A list of strings that should be treated as null. Examples: '' for empty strings, 'None', 'N/A', Warning: Hive database supports only a single value|
|» rows_to_read|body|integer \| null|false|[CSV and Excel only] Number of rows to read from the file. If None, reads all rows.|
|» schema|body|string|false|The schema to upload the data file to.|
|» sheet_name|body|string|false|[Excel only]] Strings used for sheet names (default is the first sheet).|
|» skip_blank_lines|body|boolean|false|[CSV only] Skip blank lines in the CSV file.|
|» skip_initial_space|body|boolean|false|[CSV only] Skip spaces after delimiter.|
|» skip_rows|body|integer|false|[CSV and Excel only] Number of rows to skip at start of file.|
|» table_name|body|string|true|The name of the table to be created/appended|
|» type|body|string|true|File type to upload|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» already_exists|fail|
|» already_exists|replace|
|» already_exists|append|
|» type|csv|
|» type|excel|
|» type|columnar|

> Example responses

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

## Import dataset(s) with associated databases

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/api/v1/dataset/import/ \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'formData=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'overwrite=true' \
  -F 'passwords=string' \
  -F 'ssh_tunnel_passwords=string' \
  -F 'ssh_tunnel_private_key_passwords=string' \
  -F 'ssh_tunnel_private_keys=string' \
  -F 'sync_columns=true' \
  -F 'sync_metrics=true'
```

`POST /api/v1/dataset/import/`

> Body parameter

```yaml
formData: string
overwrite: true
passwords: string
ssh_tunnel_passwords: string
ssh_tunnel_private_key_passwords: string
ssh_tunnel_private_keys: string
sync_columns: true
sync_metrics: true
```

<h3 id="import-datasets-with-associated-databases-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» formData|body|string(binary)|false|upload file (ZIP or YAML)|
|» overwrite|body|boolean|false|overwrite existing datasets?|
|» passwords|body|string|false|JSON map of passwords for each featured database in the ZIP file. If the ZIP includes a database config in the path `databases/MyDatabase.yaml`, the password should be provided in the following format: `{"databases/MyDatabase.yaml": "my_password"}`.|
|» ssh_tunnel_passwords|body|string|false|JSON map of passwords for each ssh_tunnel associated to a featured database in the ZIP file. If the ZIP includes a ssh_tunnel config in the path `databases/MyDatabase.yaml`, the password should be provided in the following format: `{"databases/MyDatabase.yaml": "my_password"}`.|
|» ssh_tunnel_private_key_passwords|body|string|false|JSON map of private_key_passwords for each ssh_tunnel associated to a featured database in the ZIP file. If the ZIP includes a ssh_tunnel config in the path `databases/MyDatabase.yaml`, the private_key should be provided in the following format: `{"databases/MyDatabase.yaml": "my_private_key_password"}`.|
|» ssh_tunnel_private_keys|body|string|false|JSON map of private_keys for each ssh_tunnel associated to a featured database in the ZIP file. If the ZIP includes a ssh_tunnel config in the path `databases/MyDatabase.yaml`, the private_key should be provided in the following format: `{"databases/MyDatabase.yaml": "my_private_key"}`.|
|» sync_columns|body|boolean|false|sync columns?|
|» sync_metrics|body|boolean|false|sync metrics?|

`GET /api/v1/dataset/related_objects/`

Aggregates the charts built on any of the requested datasets and the dashboards those charts appear on. Each chart and dashboard is listed once even if it depends on several of the datasets. Requested datasets the user cannot see are ignored; the response is 404 only when none of them are visible.

## Warm up the cache for each chart powered by the given table

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/api/v1/dataset/warm_up_cache \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "dashboard_id": 0,
    "db_name": "string",
    "extra_filters": "string",
    "table_name": "string"
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v1/dataset/warm_up_cache`

Warms up the cache for the table. Note for slices a force refresh occurs. In terms of the `extra_filters` these can be obtained from records in the JSON encoded `logs.json` column associated with the `explore` action.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "dashboard_id": 0,
  "db_name": "string",
  "extra_filters": "string",
  "table_name": "string"
}
```

|» db_name|body|string|true|The name of the database where the table is located|

<h3 id="update-a-dataset-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Dataset changed|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found|Inline|
|409|Conflict|A concurrent save on this dataset won a database lock race, so this conditional request could not be applied. The client's ``If-Match`` token is NOT proven stale: unlike a 412, the correct action is to retry the SAME request (with backoff; a few attempts, then surface the conflict) rather than refetch the entity for a new token.|Inline|
|412|Precondition Failed|The dataset changed since the version identified by the request's ``If-Match`` header; the update was not applied. The token is stale: refetch the entity to pick up the current version before retrying — retrying the same request unchanged will fail again (contrast the retryable 409 above).|Inline|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Could not process entity|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|Fatal error|Inline|

<h3 id="update-a-dataset-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|number|false|none|none|
|new_transaction_id|integer \| null|false|none|Continuum transaction_id of the live row after this update. When this differs from ``old_transaction_id`` the update produced a new version row (regardless of whether ``new_version`` changed).|
|new_version|integer \| null|false|none|0-based version_number of the newly-live row after this update. Can equal ``old_version`` when no versioned column changed, or when retention pruning dropped an older closed row in the same commit.|
|new_version_uuid|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|Deterministic version_uuid of the live row after this update. Null when version capture is disabled.|
|old_transaction_id|integer \| null|false|none|Continuum transaction_id of the live row before this update. Stable across retention pruning.|
|old_version|integer \| null|false|none|0-based version_number of the live row before this update (null if the dataset had no prior history). Matches the ``version_number`` field of the list versions endpoint. Unstable under retention pruning — see ``old_transaction_id`` for a stable identifier.|
|old_version_uuid|string(uuid) \| null|false|none|Deterministic version_uuid of the live row before this update. Null when version capture is disabled or the dataset has no version rows yet.|
|result|[DatasetRestApi.put](#schemadatasetrestapi.put)|false|none|none|

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/api/v1/dataset/0/partition_mapping/preview/ \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "is_monotonic": false,
    "mapped_column": "string",
    "operator": "==",
    "partition_column": null,
    "sample_values": [
      "string"
    ],
    "value_transform": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/dataset/{pk}/partition_mapping/preview/`

Evaluate a partition value transform at sample values and return the predicate that would be appended to queries. The predicate is built by the same code the query path uses, so the preview cannot drift from what a chart emits. Parse and denylist checks run before anything reaches the engine, so an unparseable transform costs no query.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "is_monotonic": false,
  "mapped_column": "string",
  "operator": "==",
  "partition_column": null,
  "sample_values": [
    "string"
  ],
  "value_transform": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="preview-a-partition-filter-mapping-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pk|path|integer|true|The dataset ID|
|body|body|[PartitionMappingPreviewSchema](#schemapartitionmappingpreviewschema)|true|none|
|» is_monotonic|body|boolean|false|Whether the owner has declared the transform order-preserving. Range operators only mirror when they have.|
|» mapped_column|body|string|true|Column whose filters would be mirrored|
|» operator|body|string|false|Filter operator being mirrored. Only operators the preview can construct are accepted: TEMPORAL_RANGE is mirrored by the query path as two bounds decomposed from a since/until pair, which this request has no way to express.|
|» partition_column|body|string \| null|false|Candidate partition column. The editor previews a mapping before it is saved, so this overrides the stored value; omitted, the stored one is used.|
|» sample_values|body|[string]|true|Values to evaluate the transform at. A comparison operator takes one; IN takes the whole list.|
|» value_transform|body|string \| null|true|SQL expression containing a :value placeholder|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» operator|<|
|» operator|<=|
|» operator|==|
|» operator|>|
|» operator|>=|
|» operator|IN|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": {
    "emitted_predicate": "string",
    "error": "string",
    "reason": "unconfigured",
    "sample_input": "string",
    "valid": true
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string"
}
```

```json
{
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "message": "string"
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

## Get a dataset's activity stream

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/api/v1/dataset/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/activity/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v1/dataset/{uuid_str}/activity/`

A dataset's own edits only. Datasets have no transitive layer in V2 — chart and dashboard edits that touch this dataset do NOT appear here. ``?include=self`` and ``?include=all`` return the dataset's own edits; ``?include=related`` returns an empty stream (a dataset has no related entities to fan out to).

<h3 id="get-a-datasets-activity-stream-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|uuid_str|path|string(uuid)|true|Dataset UUID|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|none|
|until|query|string(date-time)|false|none|
|include|query|string|false|none|
|q|query|string|false|Case-insensitive search over the full history (summary, entity name, kind, path, values) — applied before pagination, so `count` reflects the matches.|
|page|query|integer|false|none|
|page_size|query|integer|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|include|self|
|include|related|
|include|all|

## Query a datasource by its semantic definitions

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/api/v1/datasource/string/0/query \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "cache_timeout": null,
    "dimensions": [
      null
    ],
    "filters": [
      {
        "col": "country",
        "grain": "PT1M",
        "isExtra": true,
        "op": "IN",
        "val": [
          "China",
          "France",
          "Japan"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "force": false,
    "limit": null,
    "metrics": [
      null
    ],
    "offset": 0,
    "order": [
      {
        "column": "string",
        "descending": true
      }
    ],
    "result_format": "json",
    "semantic_selection_version": null,
    "time_column": null,
    "time_grain": null,
    "time_range": null,
    "use_cache": true
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/datasource/{datasource_type}/{datasource_id}/query`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "cache_timeout": null,
  "dimensions": [
    null
  ],
  "filters": [
    {
      "col": "country",
      "grain": "PT1M",
      "isExtra": true,
      "op": "IN",
      "val": [
        "China",
        "France",
        "Japan"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "force": false,
  "limit": null,
  "metrics": [
    null
  ],
  "offset": 0,
  "order": [
    {
      "column": "string",
      "descending": true
    }
  ],
  "result_format": "json",
  "semantic_selection_version": null,
  "time_column": null,
  "time_grain": null,
  "time_range": null,
  "use_cache": true
}
```

<h3 id="query-a-datasource-by-its-semantic-definitions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|datasource_type|path|string|true|none|
|datasource_id|path|integer|true|none|
|body|body|[DatasourceQuerySchema](#schemadatasourcequeryschema)|true|none|
|» cache_timeout|body|integer \| null|false|Seconds to cache for; -1 disables caching.|
|» dimensions|body|[object]|false|Dimension/column names to group by.|
|» filters|body|[[ChartDataFilter](#schemachartdatafilter)]|false|Filters to apply, AND-ed together.|
|» force|body|boolean|false|none|
|» limit|body|integer \| null|false|Rows to return. Also clamped server-side by ROW_LIMIT.|
|» metrics|body|[object]|false|Saved metric names, or ad-hoc metric objects (datasets only). See ChartDataAdhocMetricSchema.|
|» offset|body|integer|false|Rows to skip, for pagination.|
|» order|body|[[DatasourceQueryOrder](#schemadatasourcequeryorder)]|false|Ordering terms, applied in sequence. Each carries its own direction.|
|» result_format|body|string|false|'json' (default) or 'arrow' for an Arrow IPC stream.|
|» semantic_selection_version|body|string \| null|false|Identity version from datasource metadata, after selecting its current metric and dimension IDs. Never infer legacy IDs.|
|» time_column|body|string \| null|false|Temporal column the time range applies to. Inferred from the datasource when omitted.|
|» time_grain|body|string \| null|false|ISO 8601 duration, e.g. 'P1D' or 'PT1H'.|
|» time_range|body|string \| null|false|e.g. 'Last 30 days' or '2024-01-01 : 2024-12-31'.|
|» use_cache|body|boolean|false|none|

|Parameter|Value|

|» result_format|json|
|» result_format|xlsx|

<h1 id="superset-explore">Explore</h1>

## Assemble Explore related information in a single endpoint

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/api/v1/explore/ \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v1/explore/`

Assembles Explore related information (form_data, slice, dataset) in a single endpoint.<br/><br/> The information can be assembled from:<br/> - The cache using a form_data_key<br/> - The metadata database using a permalink_key<br/> - Build from scratch using dataset or slice identifiers.

|slice_id|query|integer|false|none|
|datasource_id|query|integer|false|none|
|datasource_type|query|string|false|none|

## Import saved queries with associated databases

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/api/v1/saved_query/import/ \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'formData=@/path/to/file' \
  -F 'overwrite=true' \
  -F 'passwords=string' \
  -F 'ssh_tunnel_passwords=string' \
  -F 'ssh_tunnel_private_key_passwords=string' \
  -F 'ssh_tunnel_private_keys=string'
```

`POST /api/v1/saved_query/import/`

> Body parameter

```yaml
formData: string
overwrite: true
passwords: string
ssh_tunnel_passwords: string
ssh_tunnel_private_key_passwords: string
ssh_tunnel_private_keys: string
```

<h3 id="import-saved-queries-with-associated-databases-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» formData|body|string(binary)|false|upload file (ZIP)|
|» overwrite|body|boolean|false|overwrite existing saved queries?|
|» passwords|body|string|false|JSON map of passwords for each featured database in the ZIP file. If the ZIP includes a database config in the path `databases/MyDatabase.yaml`, the password should be provided in the following format: `{"databases/MyDatabase.yaml": "my_password"}`.|
|» ssh_tunnel_passwords|body|string|false|JSON map of passwords for each ssh_tunnel associated to a featured database in the ZIP file. If the ZIP includes a ssh_tunnel config in the path `databases/MyDatabase.yaml`, the password should be provided in the following format: `{"databases/MyDatabase.yaml": "my_password"}`.|
|» ssh_tunnel_private_key_passwords|body|string|false|JSON map of private_key_passwords for each ssh_tunnel associated to a featured database in the ZIP file. If the ZIP includes a ssh_tunnel config in the path `databases/MyDatabase.yaml`, the private_key should be provided in the following format: `{"databases/MyDatabase.yaml": "my_private_key_password"}`.|
|» ssh_tunnel_private_keys|body|string|false|JSON map of private_keys for each ssh_tunnel associated to a featured database in the ZIP file. If the ZIP includes a ssh_tunnel config in the path `databases/MyDatabase.yaml`, the private_key should be provided in the following format: `{"databases/MyDatabase.yaml": "my_private_key"}`.|

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

|» column_name|string|false|none|The label for the column name. Will be translated by babel|

## Create a report schedule

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/api/v1/report/ \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "active": true,
    "chart": 0,
    "context_markdown": "string",
    "creation_method": "charts",
    "crontab": "*/5 * * * *",
    "custom_width": 1000,
    "dashboard": 0,
    "database": 0,
    "description": "Daily sales dashboard to marketing",
    "editors": [
      0
    ],
    "email_subject": "[Report]  Report name: Dashboard or chart name",
    "extra": {},
    "force_screenshot": true,
    "grace_period": 14400,
    "include_cta": true,
    "log_retention": 90,
    "name": "Daily dashboard email",
    "recipients": [
      {
        "recipient_config_json": {
          "bccTarget": "string",
          "ccTarget": "string",
          "target": "string"
        },
        "type": "Email"
      }
    ],
    "report_format": "PDF",
    "retry_max_attempts": 3,
    "retry_notify_owners": true,
    "retry_notify_recipients": false,
    "retry_on_failure": false,
    "run_alert_query_as": 0,
    "run_alert_query_as_type": "fixed_user",
    "run_as": 0,
    "run_as_type": "fixed_user",
    "send_failed_reports": false,
    "sql": "SELECT value FROM time_series_table",
    "timezone": "Africa/Abidjan",
    "type": "Alert",
    "validator_config_json": {
      "op": "<",
      "threshold": 0
    },
    "validator_type": "not null",
    "working_timeout": 3600
  }'
```

<h3 id="create-a-report-schedule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ReportScheduleRestApi.post](#schemareportschedulerestapi.post)|true|Report Schedule schema|
|» active|body|boolean|false|none|
|» chart|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» context_markdown|body|string \| null|false|Markdown description|
|» creation_method|body|string|false|Creation method is used to inform the frontend whether the report/alert was created in the dashboard, chart, or alerts and reports UI.|
|» crontab|body|string|true|A CRON expression.[Crontab Guru](https://crontab.guru/) is a helpful resource that can help you craft a CRON expression.|
|» custom_width|body|integer \| null|false|Custom width of the screenshot in pixels|
|» dashboard|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» database|body|integer|false|none|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Use a nice description to give context to this Alert/Report|
|» editors|body|[integer \| object]|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|Subject ID, not a user ID.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » id|body|integer|true|none|
|» » type|body|string|true|none|
|» email_subject|body|string \| null|false|The report schedule subject line|
|» extra|body|object|false|none|
|» force_screenshot|body|boolean|false|none|
|» grace_period|body|integer|false|Once an alert is triggered, how long, in seconds, before Superset nags you again. (in seconds)|
|» include_cta|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether to include the call-to-action link back to Superset (e.g. 'Explore in Superset') in the delivered notifications|
|» log_retention|body|integer|false|How long to keep the logs around for this report (in days)|
|» name|body|string|true|The report schedule name.|
|» recipients|body|[[ReportRecipient](#schemareportrecipient)]|false|none|
|» report_format|body|string|false|Attachment format. NONE disables attachments for alerts and makes chart/dashboard optional. Omitted attachment settings are preserved on update.|
|» retry_max_attempts|body|integer|false|Maximum number of retry attempts (1–10)|
|» retry_notify_owners|body|boolean|false|Notify report owners on each retry attempt|
|» retry_notify_recipients|body|boolean|false|Notify report recipients on each retry attempt|
|» retry_on_failure|body|boolean|false|Enable automatic retries on report failure|
|» run_alert_query_as|body|integer \| null|false|ID of the user whose credentials are used when running the alert condition SQL query, useful when the audience of the alert does not have access to the database. Null inherits the content executor at execution time.|
|» run_alert_query_as_type|body|string \| null|false|Alert query executor type; null inherits run_as.|
|» run_as|body|integer \| null|false|ID of the user whose credentials (RBAC permissions, database OAuth2 tokens) are used when rendering the content (screenshot, PDF, CSV, XLSX or text). Admins can set any active user; non-admins can only set themselves. Onlyhonored when the ALERT_REPORT_DYNAMIC_EXECUTOR feature flag is enabled. Admins can set this and run_as_type to null to use ALERT_REPORTS_EXECUTORS.|
|» run_as_type|body|string \| null|false|Explicit executor type; fixed_user requires run_as.|
|» send_failed_reports|body|boolean|false|Send the failed report to all recipients after retries are exhausted|
|» sql|body|string|false|A SQL statement that defines whether the alert should get triggered or not. The query is expected to return either NULL or a number value.|
|» timezone|body|string|false|A timezone string that represents the location of the timezone.|
|» type|body|string|true|The report schedule type|
|» validator_config_json|body|[ValidatorConfigJSON](#schemavalidatorconfigjson)|false|none|
|» validator_type|body|string|false|Determines when to trigger alert based off value from alert query. Alerts will be triggered with these validator types:<br>- Not Null - When the return value is Not NULL, Empty, or 0<br>- Operator - When `sql_return_value comparison_operator threshold` is True e.g. `50 <= 75`<br>Supports the comparison operators <, <=, >, >=, ==, and !=|
|» working_timeout|body|integer|false|If an alert is staled at a working state, how long until it's state is reset to error|

## Update the global Alerts &amp; Reports configuration

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/api/v1/report/configuration/ \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "alert_minimum_interval": 3600,
    "alerts_attach_reports": true,
    "allowed_email_domains": [
      "example.com",
      "superset.com"
    ],
    "date_format_in_email_subject": true,
    "limit_recipients_to_users": true,
    "report_minimum_interval": 3600
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v1/report/configuration/`

Admin only. Absent fields keep their value and ``null`` clears a field without restoring its legacy fallback. Recipient restrictions and minimum intervals are validated against existing alerts/reports. When any conflicts, the configuration is not saved and the impacted schedules are returned.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "alert_minimum_interval": 3600,
  "alerts_attach_reports": true,
  "allowed_email_domains": [
    "example.com",
    "superset.com"
  ],
  "date_format_in_email_subject": true,
  "limit_recipients_to_users": true,
  "report_minimum_interval": 3600
}
```

<h3 id="update-the-global-alerts-reports-configuration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ReportConfigurationSchema](#schemareportconfigurationschema)|true|Alerts & Reports configuration|
|» alert_minimum_interval|body|integer \| null|false|Minimum interval between alert executions, in seconds. Values below 120 do not restrict schedules. Falls back to ALERT_MINIMUM_INTERVAL only before this setting has been saved.|
|» alerts_attach_reports|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether alerts deliver their attachment (screenshot, PDF, CSV or XLSX). When disabled, alerts only send the message and link. Falls back to the FF until a row has first been saved.|
|» allowed_email_domains|body|[string]|false|E-mail domains accepted as recipients. An empty list allows any domain.|
|» date_format_in_email_subject|body|boolean \| null|false|Render strftime date placeholders in email subjects. Falls back to the DATE_FORMAT_IN_EMAIL_SUBJECT FF until first saved.|
|» limit_recipients_to_users|body|boolean \| null|false|When enabled, only e-mail addresses of existing active users are accepted as recipients.|
|» report_minimum_interval|body|integer \| null|false|Minimum interval between report executions, in seconds. Values below 120 do not restrict schedules. Falls back to REPORT_MINIMUM_INTERVAL only before this setting has been saved.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "result": {
    "alert_minimum_interval": 3600,
    "alerts_attach_reports": true,
    "allowed_email_domains": [
      "example.com",
      "superset.com"
    ],
    "date_format_in_email_subject": true,
    "limit_recipients_to_users": true,
    "report_minimum_interval": 3600
  }
}
```

```json
  "message": "string"
}
```

## Subscribe to a chart or dashboard report

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/api/v1/report/subscribe \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "active": true,
    "chart": 0,
    "context_markdown": "string",
    "creation_method": "charts",
    "crontab": "*/5 * * * *",
    "custom_width": 1000,
    "dashboard": 0,
    "database": 0,
    "description": "Daily sales dashboard to marketing",
    "editors": [
      0
    ],
    "email_subject": "[Report]  Report name: Dashboard or chart name",
    "extra": {},
    "force_screenshot": true,
    "grace_period": 14400,
    "include_cta": true,
    "log_retention": 90,
    "name": "Daily dashboard email",
    "recipients": [
      {
        "recipient_config_json": {
          "bccTarget": "string",
          "ccTarget": "string",
          "target": "string"
        },
        "type": "Email"
      }
    ],
    "report_format": "PDF",
    "retry_max_attempts": 3,
    "retry_notify_owners": true,
    "retry_notify_recipients": false,
    "retry_on_failure": false,
    "run_alert_query_as": 0,
    "run_alert_query_as_type": "fixed_user",
    "run_as": 0,
    "run_as_type": "fixed_user",
    "send_failed_reports": false,
    "sql": "SELECT value FROM time_series_table",
    "timezone": "Africa/Abidjan",
    "type": "Alert",
    "validator_config_json": {
      "op": "<",
      "threshold": 0
    },
    "validator_type": "not null",
    "working_timeout": 3600
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/report/subscribe`

Creates a report schedule locked to the authenticated user's email. ``creation_method`` is derived server-side from the payload (chart → charts, dashboard → dashboards). ``recipients`` are not accepted and are always set to the requesting user's email address.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "chart": 0,
  "context_markdown": "string",
  "creation_method": "charts",
  "crontab": "*/5 * * * *",
  "custom_width": 1000,
  "dashboard": 0,
  "database": 0,
  "description": "Daily sales dashboard to marketing",
  "editors": [
    0
  ],
  "email_subject": "[Report]  Report name: Dashboard or chart name",
  "extra": {},
  "force_screenshot": true,
  "grace_period": 14400,
  "include_cta": true,
  "log_retention": 90,
  "name": "Daily dashboard email",
  "recipients": [
    {
      "recipient_config_json": {
        "bccTarget": "string",
        "ccTarget": "string",
        "target": "string"
      },
      "type": "Email"
    }
  ],
  "report_format": "PDF",
  "retry_max_attempts": 3,
  "retry_notify_owners": true,
  "retry_notify_recipients": false,
  "retry_on_failure": false,
  "run_alert_query_as": 0,
  "run_alert_query_as_type": "fixed_user",
  "run_as": 0,
  "run_as_type": "fixed_user",
  "send_failed_reports": false,
  "sql": "SELECT value FROM time_series_table",
  "timezone": "Africa/Abidjan",
  "type": "Alert",
  "validator_config_json": {
    "op": "<",
    "threshold": 0
  },
  "validator_type": "not null",
  "working_timeout": 3600
}
```

<h3 id="subscribe-to-a-chart-or-dashboard-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ReportScheduleRestApi.post](#schemareportschedulerestapi.post)|true|Report schedule subscription schema|
|» active|body|boolean|false|none|
|» chart|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» context_markdown|body|string \| null|false|Markdown description|
|» creation_method|body|string|false|Creation method is used to inform the frontend whether the report/alert was created in the dashboard, chart, or alerts and reports UI.|
|» crontab|body|string|true|A CRON expression.[Crontab Guru](https://crontab.guru/) is a helpful resource that can help you craft a CRON expression.|
|» custom_width|body|integer \| null|false|Custom width of the screenshot in pixels|
|» dashboard|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» database|body|integer|false|none|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|Use a nice description to give context to this Alert/Report|
|» editors|body|[integer \| object]|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|Subject ID, not a user ID.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» » id|body|integer|true|none|
|» » type|body|string|true|none|
|» email_subject|body|string \| null|false|The report schedule subject line|
|» extra|body|object|false|none|
|» force_screenshot|body|boolean|false|none|
|» grace_period|body|integer|false|Once an alert is triggered, how long, in seconds, before Superset nags you again. (in seconds)|
|» include_cta|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether to include the call-to-action link back to Superset (e.g. 'Explore in Superset') in the delivered notifications|
|» log_retention|body|integer|false|How long to keep the logs around for this report (in days)|
|» name|body|string|true|The report schedule name.|
|» recipients|body|[[ReportRecipient](#schemareportrecipient)]|false|none|
|» report_format|body|string|false|Attachment format. NONE disables attachments for alerts and makes chart/dashboard optional. Omitted attachment settings are preserved on update.|
|» retry_max_attempts|body|integer|false|Maximum number of retry attempts (1–10)|
|» retry_notify_owners|body|boolean|false|Notify report owners on each retry attempt|
|» retry_notify_recipients|body|boolean|false|Notify report recipients on each retry attempt|
|» retry_on_failure|body|boolean|false|Enable automatic retries on report failure|
|» run_alert_query_as|body|integer \| null|false|ID of the user whose credentials are used when running the alert condition SQL query, useful when the audience of the alert does not have access to the database. Null inherits the content executor at execution time.|
|» run_alert_query_as_type|body|string \| null|false|Alert query executor type; null inherits run_as.|
|» run_as|body|integer \| null|false|ID of the user whose credentials (RBAC permissions, database OAuth2 tokens) are used when rendering the content (screenshot, PDF, CSV, XLSX or text). Admins can set any active user; non-admins can only set themselves. Onlyhonored when the ALERT_REPORT_DYNAMIC_EXECUTOR feature flag is enabled. Admins can set this and run_as_type to null to use ALERT_REPORTS_EXECUTORS.|
|» run_as_type|body|string \| null|false|Explicit executor type; fixed_user requires run_as.|
|» send_failed_reports|body|boolean|false|Send the failed report to all recipients after retries are exhausted|
|» sql|body|string|false|A SQL statement that defines whether the alert should get triggered or not. The query is expected to return either NULL or a number value.|
|» timezone|body|string|false|A timezone string that represents the location of the timezone.|
|» type|body|string|true|The report schedule type|
|» validator_config_json|body|[ValidatorConfigJSON](#schemavalidatorconfigjson)|false|none|
|» validator_type|body|string|false|Determines when to trigger alert based off value from alert query. Alerts will be triggered with these validator types:<br>- Not Null - When the return value is Not NULL, Empty, or 0<br>- Operator - When `sql_return_value comparison_operator threshold` is True e.g. `50 <= 75`<br>Supports the comparison operators <, <=, >, >=, ==, and !=|
|» working_timeout|body|integer|false|If an alert is staled at a working state, how long until it's state is reset to error|

|» include_cta|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether to include the call-to-action link back to Superset (e.g. 'Explore in Superset') in the delivered notifications|
|» log_retention|body|integer|false|How long to keep the logs around for this report (in days)|
|» name|body|string|false|The report schedule name.|

|» report_format|body|string|false|Attachment format. NONE disables attachments for alerts and makes chart/dashboard optional. Omitted attachment settings are preserved on update.|
|» retry_max_attempts|body|integer|false|Maximum number of retry attempts (1–10)|
|» retry_notify_owners|body|boolean|false|Notify report owners on each retry attempt|
|» retry_notify_recipients|body|boolean|false|Notify report recipients on each retry attempt|
|» retry_on_failure|body|boolean|false|Enable automatic retries on report failure|
|» run_alert_query_as|body|integer \| null|false|ID of the user whose credentials are used when running the alert condition SQL query, useful when the audience of the alert does not have access to the database. Null inherits the content executor at execution time.|
|» run_alert_query_as_type|body|string \| null|false|Alert query executor type; null inherits run_as.|
|» run_as|body|integer \| null|false|ID of the user whose credentials (RBAC permissions, database OAuth2 tokens) are used when rendering the content (screenshot, PDF, CSV, XLSX or text). Admins can set any active user; non-admins can only set themselves. Onlyhonored when the ALERT_REPORT_DYNAMIC_EXECUTOR feature flag is enabled. Admins can set this and run_as_type to null to use ALERT_REPORTS_EXECUTORS.|
|» run_as_type|body|string \| null|false|Explicit executor type; fixed_user requires run_as.|
|» send_failed_reports|body|boolean|false|Send the failed report to all recipients after retries are exhausted|
|» sql|body|string \| null|false|A SQL statement that defines whether the alert should get triggered or not. The query is expected to return either NULL or a number value.|
|» timezone|body|string|false|A timezone string that represents the location of the timezone.|
|» type|body|string|false|The report schedule type|
|» validator_config_json|body|[ValidatorConfigJSON](#schemavalidatorconfigjson)|false|none|
|» validator_type|body|string \| null|false|Determines when to trigger alert based off value from alert query. Alerts will be triggered with these validator types:<br>- Not Null - When the return value is Not NULL, Empty, or 0<br>- Operator - When `sql_return_value comparison_operator threshold` is True e.g. `50 <= 75`<br>Supports the comparison operators <, <=, >, >=, ==, and !=|
|» working_timeout|body|integer \| null|false|If an alert is staled at a working state, how long until it's state is reset to error|

```bash
  -X POST \
```
```bash
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "clause": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "filter_type": "Regular",
    "group_key": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "subjects": [
      0
    ],
    "tables": [
      0
    ]
```

## Get the resolved system default and dark themes

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8088/api/v1/theme/system \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v1/theme/system`

Returns the same processed theme payload embedded in the page bootstrap: the resolved system default and dark themes, the default mode, and the UI theme administration flag. The client uses this to apply system theme changes live without a full page reload, keeping the result identical to what a reload would render.
