# Schemas

<h2 id="tocS_ActivityChangedBy">ActivityChangedBy</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaactivitychangedby"></a>
<a id="schema_ActivityChangedBy"></a>
<a id="tocSactivitychangedby"></a>
<a id="tocsactivitychangedby"></a>

```json
{
  "first_name": "string",
  "id": 0,
  "last_name": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|first_name|string|false|none|none|
|id|integer|false|none|none|
|last_name|string|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_ActivityImpact">ActivityImpact</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaactivityimpact"></a>
<a id="schema_ActivityImpact"></a>
<a id="tocSactivityimpact"></a>
<a id="tocsactivityimpact"></a>

```json
{
  "affected_charts": [
    {
      "id": 0,
      "name": "string"
    }
  ],
  "charts": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|affected_charts|[[ActivityImpactChart](#schemaactivityimpactchart)]|false|none|The affected sibling charts (id + name), sorted by name — the detail behind the ``charts`` count, rendered as the rollup entry's hover tooltip. Capped at 50 entries per record; ``charts`` always carries the full count.|
|charts|integer|false|none|Number of sibling charts on the path entity affected by the same related-record change at this transaction.|

<h2 id="tocS_ActivityImpactChart">ActivityImpactChart</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaactivityimpactchart"></a>
<a id="schema_ActivityImpactChart"></a>
<a id="tocSactivityimpactchart"></a>
<a id="tocsactivityimpactchart"></a>

```json
{
  "id": 0,
  "name": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer|false|none|Chart id.|
|name|string|false|none|Chart name at the change's transaction — it may differ from the live name if the chart was renamed since.|

<h2 id="tocS_ActivityRecord">ActivityRecord</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaactivityrecord"></a>
<a id="schema_ActivityRecord"></a>
<a id="tocSactivityrecord"></a>
<a id="tocsactivityrecord"></a>

```json
{
  "action_kind": "clone",
  "changed_by": {
    "first_name": "string",
    "id": 0,
    "last_name": "string"
  },
  "creation_kind": "pre_tracking",
  "entity_deleted": true,
  "entity_deletion_state": "soft_deleted",
  "entity_kind": "dashboard",
  "entity_name": "string",
  "entity_uuid": "string",
  "first_tracked_save": true,
  "from_value": null,
  "impact": {
    "affected_charts": [
      {
        "id": 0,
        "name": "string"
      }
    ],
    "charts": 0
  },
  "issued_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "kind": "filter",
  "operation": "add",
  "path": [
    "string"
  ],
  "source": "self",
  "summary": "string",
  "to_value": null,
  "transaction_id": 0,
  "version_uuid": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|action_kind|string \| null|false|none|Transaction-level avenue that produced this record's batch: ``restore`` / ``import`` / ``clone``. ``null`` for ordinary saves. All records sharing a ``transaction_id`` share the same action_kind. The schema's third ``*_kind`` column (entity_kind / kind / action_kind), at transaction scope.|
|changed_by|object \| null|false|none|User who produced the change, or ``null`` when the saving user no longer exists in ``ab_user``.|
|creation_kind|string \| null|false|none|Set only on the synthetic starting-version record (``kind == "__creation__"``): how the entity came to exist. ``"pre_tracking"`` — a retroactive baseline for an entity that predates versioning; ``"created"`` — a creation with tracking on; ``"imported"`` — an import, attributed to the importing user; ``"unknown"`` — an unstamped starting version whose creation provenance cannot be established. Machine values: display copy is owned by the client.|
|entity_deleted|boolean|false|none|True iff the source entity is hard-deleted (no live row by ``entity_id``). False for live and soft-deleted entities.|
|entity_deletion_state|string \| null|false|none|Present when the source entity has non-null ``deleted_at`` Absent or ``null`` otherwise.|
|entity_kind|string|false|none|User-facing kind of the source entity: one of ``"dashboard"`` / ``"chart"`` / ``"dataset"``.|
|entity_name|string|false|none|Name of the source entity *at the time of the change* — denormalized from the validity-strategy shadow row. Survives entity rename / delete.|
|entity_uuid|string \| null|false|none|UUID of the source entity; ``null`` only when ``entity_deleted: true`` (the entity has been hard-deleted since the change was recorded).|
|first_tracked_save|boolean|false|none|True when this record's transaction is the entity's FIRST tracked save (first UPDATE after the retroactive baseline). Such transactions can carry dozens of params-normalization records for entities that predate versioning; clients use the marker to collapse them rather than render each delta as a user edit. Matched against the LIVE row's (id, uuid), so it is always false for hard-deleted entities (no live row) and for shadow rows predating the entity's current uuid.|
|from_value|object \| null|false|none|Prior value; ``null`` = didn't exist.|
|impact|object \| null|false|none|Optional dependent-count for ``source: "related"`` records — e.g., ``{"charts": 4}`` for a dataset edit that affected 4 charts on the path dashboard at the change's transaction. Absent for ``source: "self"`` records and for related records without dependents.|
|issued_at|string(date-time)|false|none|UTC timestamp; primary ordering key (DESC).|
|kind|string|false|none|Content category — what kind of thing changed. ``field`` is the fallback for scalar changes without a more specific category. Per-record.|
|operation|string|false|none|Per-record verb: ``add`` / ``remove`` / ``move`` / ``edit``. Explicit instead of inferred from ``from_value`` / ``to_value`` null-tests. ``move`` only fires for layout records.|
|path|[string]|false|none|Pure navigation address — no verb or kind embedded. Examples: ``['slice_name']``, ``['params', 'adhoc_filters', 'country']``, ``['CHART-x']`` for a layout add/remove/move, ``['HEADER-y', 'text']`` for a layout edit leaf. The verb lives in ``operation``, the element type in ``kind``.|
|source|string|false|none|``"self"`` if ``(entity_kind, entity_id)`` matches the path entity; else ``"related"``. Drives the frontend's no-group-under-save rendering rule.|
|summary|string|false|none|Synthesized headline for ``source: "related"`` records — e.g., ``"Dataset updated: Sales Transactions"``. Empty string for ``source: "self"`` records, except ``__meta__`` self records (e.g. restore announcements), which carry their own headline.|
|to_value|object \| null|false|none|New value; ``null`` = removed.|
|transaction_id|integer|false|none|Stable secondary ordering key; never reused.|
|version_uuid|string|false|none|Stable UUIDv5 identifier for the source version (``derive_version_uuid(entity_uuid, transaction_id)``). Identical to what ``/versions/<version_uuid>/`` would return for the same change.|

```json
{
  "aggregate": "AVG",
  "column": {
    "column_name": "mycol",
    "type": "BIGINT"
  },
  "expressionType": "SQL",
  "hasCustomLabel": true,
  "isExtra": true,
  "label": "Weighted observations",
  "optionName": "metric_aec60732-fac0-4b17-b736-93f1a5c93e30",
  "sqlExpression": "SUM(weight * observations) / SUM(weight)",
  "timeGrain": "PT1M"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggregate|string|false|none|Aggregation operator.Only required for simple expression types.|
|column|[ChartDataColumn](#schemachartdatacolumn)|false|none|none|
|expressionType|string|true|none|Simple or SQL metric|
|hasCustomLabel|boolean|false|none|When false, the label will be automatically generated based on the aggregate expression. When true, a custom label has to be specified.|
|isExtra|boolean|false|none|Indicates if the filter has been added by a filter component as opposed to being a part of the original query.|
|label|string|false|none|Label for the metric. Is automatically generated unlesshasCustomLabel is true, in which case label must be defined.|
|optionName|string|false|none|Unique identifier. Can be any string value, as long as all metrics have a unique identifier. If undefined, a random namewill be generated.|
|sqlExpression|string|false|none|The metric as defined by a SQL aggregate expression. Only required for SQL expression type.|
|timeGrain|string|false|none|Optional time grain for temporal filters|

|aggregate|SUM|
|aggregate|MEDIAN|
|aggregate|STDDEV_SAMP|
|aggregate|VAR_SAMP|
|expressionType|SIMPLE|
|expressionType|SQL|

<h2 id="tocS_ChartDataAggregateOptionsSchema">ChartDataAggregateOptionsSchema</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemachartdataaggregateoptionsschema"></a>
<a id="schema_ChartDataAggregateOptionsSchema"></a>
<a id="tocSchartdataaggregateoptionsschema"></a>
<a id="tocschartdataaggregateoptionsschema"></a>

```json
{
  "aggregates": {
    "first_quantile": {
      "column": "my_col",
      "operator": "percentile",
      "options": {
        "q": 0.25
      }
    }
  },
  "groupby": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|aggregates|object|false|none|The keys are the name of the aggregate column to be created, and the values specify the details of how to apply the aggregation. If an operator requires additional options, these can be passed here to be unpacked in the operator call. The following numpy operators are supported: average, argmin, argmax, cumsum, cumprod, max, mean, median, nansum, nanmin, nanmax, nanmean, nanmedian, min, percentile, prod, product, std, sum, var. Any options required by the operator can be passed to the `options` object.<br><br>In the example, a new column `first_quantile` is created based on values in the column `my_col` using the `percentile` operator with the `q=0.25` parameter.|
|groupby|[string]|true|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_ChartDataAsyncResponseSchema">ChartDataAsyncResponseSchema</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemachartdataasyncresponseschema"></a>
<a id="schema_ChartDataAsyncResponseSchema"></a>
<a id="tocSchartdataasyncresponseschema"></a>
<a id="tocschartdataasyncresponseschema"></a>

```json
{
  "cursor": "string",
  "tab_id": "string",
  "task_ids": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cursor|string|false|none|Status-changes recovery cursor captured before any task was created. The client polls `/api/v1/task/status_changes` from it and is guaranteed to observe each task's completion.|
|tab_id|string \| null|false|none|The per-client (e.g. browser-tab) id echoed back when the caller advertised one, so a later cancel detaches exactly that client. Absent when the caller supplied none.|
|task_ids|[string]|false|none|UUIDs of the scheduled GTF tasks (one per QueryObject that missed the cache), in query order. The client polls `/api/v1/task/status_changes`, aggregates these tasks' statuses, and re-issues this request once they all succeed.|

The following numpy operators are supported: average, argmin, argmax, cumsum, cumprod, max, mean, median, nansum, nanmin, nanmax, nanmean, nanmedian, min, percentile, prod, product, std, sum, var. Any options required by the operator can be passed to the `options` object.<br><br>In the example, a new column `first_quantile` is created based on values in the column `my_col` using the `percentile` operator with the `q=0.25` parameter.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|async_mode|boolean \| null|false|none|Opt this request into asynchronous execution on the Global Task Framework (requires the GLOBAL_ASYNC_QUERIES feature flag). When true the response is HTTP 202 with the query task ids to poll; when absent or false the query runs synchronously (HTTP 200). Default: `false`.|
|custom_cache_timeout|integer \| null|false|none|Override the default cache timeout|
|datasource|[ChartDataDatasource](#schemachartdatadatasource)|false|none|none|
|force|boolean \| null|false|none|Should the queries be forced to load from the source. Default: `false`|
|force_nonce|string \| null|false|none|Forced-refresh idempotency token for a single-query request: the async task's UUID (as returned in the 202 `task_ids`). Sent on the synchronous read-back of a forced refresh so it reads the result the task warmed instead of recomputing; concurrent refreshes joining the same shared task read back under the same token. Multi-query requests set the per-query `force_nonce` on each query instead. Ignored when `force` is false.|
|form_data|object \| null|false|none|none|
|queries|[[ChartDataQueryObject](#schemachartdataqueryobject)]|false|none|none|
|result_format|string|false|none|none|
|result_type|string|false|none|none|
|tab_id|string \| null|false|none|Opaque per-browser-tab id (see the frontend `getTabId`). On an async request it ref-counts this tab as a consumer of the shared chart-data task so a cancel/navigate-away from one tab doesn't abort a task another tab still awaits. Read by the API as a request-level routing hint; not part of the query context.|

|grouping_sets|[[string]]|false|none|Rollup levels for non-additive totals: each entry is the list of groupby columns to group at that level (e.g. the empty list is the grand total). When set and the engine supports it, the levels are computed in a single GROUPING SETS query.|
|having|string \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** HAVING clause to be added to aggregate queries using AND operator. This field is deprecated and should be passed to `extras`.|
|is_rowcount|boolean \| null|false|none|Should the rowcount of the actual query be returned|

|order_desc|boolean \| null|false|none|Reverse order. Default: `false`|
|orderby|[object]|false|none|Expects a list of lists where the first element is the column name which to sort by, and the second element is a boolean.|
|post_processing|[object \| null]|false|none|Post processing operations to be applied to the result set. Operations are applied to the result set in sequential order.|
|result_type|string \| null|false|none|none|
|row_limit|integer \| null|false|none|Maximum row count (0=disabled). Default: `config["ROW_LIMIT"]`|
|row_offset|integer \| null|false|none|Number of rows to skip. Default: `0`|
|series_columns|[object]|false|none|Columns to use when limiting series count. All columns must be present in the `columns` property. Requires `series_limit` and `series_limit_metric` to be set.|
|series_limit|integer \| null|false|none|Maximum number of series. Requires `series` and `series_limit_metric` to be set.|
|series_limit_metric|object \| null|false|none|Metric used to limit timeseries queries by. Requires `series` and `series_limit` to be set.|
|time_compare_full_range|boolean \| null|false|none|When using a time comparison (time_offsets), plot each shifted series across its full time range instead of truncating it to the main series' range. Useful for comparing a partial current period against complete prior periods.|
|time_offsets|[string]|false|none|none|
|time_range|string \| null|false|none|A time rage, either expressed as a colon separated string `since : until` or human readable freeform. Valid formats for `since` and `until` are: <br>- ISO 8601<br>- X days/years/hours/day/year/weeks<br>- X days/years/hours/day/year/weeks ago<br>- X days/years/hours/day/year/weeks from now<br><br>Additionally, the following freeform can be used:<br><br>- Last day<br>- Last week<br>- Last month<br>- Last quarter<br>- Last year<br>- No filter<br>- Last X seconds/minutes/hours/days/weeks/months/years<br>- Next X seconds/minutes/hours/days/weeks/months/years<br>|
|time_shift|string \| null|false|none|A human-readable date/time string. Please refer to [parsdatetime](https://github.com/bear/parsedatetime) documentation for details on valid values.|
|timeseries_limit|integer \| null|false|none|Maximum row count for timeseries queries. This field is deprecated, use `series_limit` instead.Default: `0`|
|timeseries_limit_metric|object \| null|false|none|Metric used to limit timeseries queries by. This field is deprecated, use `series_limit_metric` instead.|
|url_params|object \| null|false|none|Optional query parameters passed to a dashboard or Explore  view|
|where|string \| null|false|none|**Deprecated.** WHERE clause to be added to queries using AND operator.This field is deprecated and should be passed to `extras`.|

<h2 id="tocS_ChartDataRollingOptionsSchema">ChartDataRollingOptionsSchema</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemachartdatarollingoptionsschema"></a>
<a id="schema_ChartDataRollingOptionsSchema"></a>
<a id="tocSchartdatarollingoptionsschema"></a>
<a id="tocschartdatarollingoptionsschema"></a>

```json
{
  "center": false,
  "columns": {
    "sales": "weekly_rolling_sales"
  },
  "min_periods": 7,
  "rolling_type": "percentile",
  "rolling_type_options": {},
  "win_type": "boxcar",
  "window": 7
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|center|boolean|false|none|Should the label be at the center of the window.Default: `false`|
|columns|object|true|none|columns on which to perform rolling, mapping source column to target column. For instance, `{'y': 'y'}` will replace the column `y` with the rolling value in `y`, while `{'y': 'y2'}` will add a column `y2` based on rolling values calculated from `y`, leaving the original column `y` unchanged.|
|min_periods|integer|false|none|The minimum amount of periods required for a row to be included in the result set.|
|rolling_type|string|true|none|Type of rolling window. Any numpy function will work.|
|rolling_type_options|object|false|none|Optional options to pass to rolling method. Needed for e.g. quantile operation.|
|win_type|string|false|none|Type of window function. See [SciPy window functions](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference /signal.windows.html#module-scipy.signal.windows) for more details. Some window functions require passing additional parameters to `rolling_type_options`. For instance, to use `gaussian`, the parameter `std` needs to be provided.|
|window|integer|true|none|Size of the rolling window in days.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|rolling_type|average|
|rolling_type|argmin|
|rolling_type|argmax|

|rolling_type|var|
|win_type|boxcar|
|win_type|triang|
|win_type|blackman|
|win_type|hamming|
|win_type|bartlett|
|win_type|parzen|

|win_type|barthann|
|win_type|kaiser|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|allow_ctas|boolean|false|none|Allow CREATE TABLE AS option in SQL Lab|
|allow_cvas|boolean|false|none|Allow CREATE VIEW AS option in SQL Lab|
|allow_dml|boolean|false|none|Allow users to run non-SELECT statements (UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE, ...) in SQL Lab|
|allow_file_upload|boolean|false|none|Allow to upload CSV file data into this databaseIf selected, please set the schemas allowed for csv upload in Extra.|
|allow_run_async|boolean|false|none|Operate the database in asynchronous mode, meaning that the queries are executed on remote workers as opposed to on the web server itself. This assumes that you have a Celery worker setup as well as a results backend. Refer to the installation docs for more information.|
|backend|string \| null|false|none|SQLAlchemy engine to use|
|cache_timeout|integer \| null|false|none|Duration (in seconds) of the caching timeout for charts of this database. A timeout of 0 indicates that the cache never expires, and -1 bypasses the cache. Note this defaults to the global timeout if undefined.|
|configuration_method|string|false|none|Configuration_method is used on the frontend to inform the backend whether to explode parameters or to provide only a sqlalchemy_uri.|
|database_name|string \| null|false|none|A database name to identify this connection.|
|driver|string \| null|false|none|SQLAlchemy driver to use|
|engine_information|[EngineInformation](#schemaengineinformation)|false|none|none|
|expose_in_sqllab|boolean|false|none|Expose this database to SQLLab|
|extra|string|false|none|<p>JSON string containing extra configuration elements.<br>1. The <code>engine_params</code> object gets unpacked into the <a href="https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/core/engines.html#sqlalchemy.create_engine" rel="noopener noreferrer">sqlalchemy.create_engine</a> call, while the <code>metadata_params</code> gets unpacked into the <a href="https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/rel_1_0/core/metadata.html#sqlalchemy.schema.MetaData" rel="noopener noreferrer">sqlalchemy.MetaData</a> call.<br>2. The <code>metadata_cache_timeout</code> is a cache timeout setting in seconds for metadata fetch of this database. Specify it as <strong>"metadata_cache_timeout": {"schema_cache_timeout": 600, "table_cache_timeout": 600}</strong>. If unset, cache will not be enabled for the functionality. A timeout of 0 indicates that the cache never expires.<br>3. The <code>schemas_allowed_for_file_upload</code> is a comma separated list of schemas that CSVs are allowed to upload to. Specify it as <strong>"schemas_allowed_for_file_upload": ["public", "csv_upload"]</strong>. If database flavor does not support schema or any schema is allowed to be accessed, just leave the list empty<br>4. The <code>version</code> field is a string specifying the this db's version. This should be used with Presto DBs so that the syntax is correct<br>5. The <code>allows_virtual_table_explore</code> field is a boolean specifying whether or not the Explore button in SQL Lab results is shown.<br>6. The <code>disable_data_preview</code> field is a boolean specifying whether or not data preview queries will be run when fetching table metadata in SQL Lab.<br>7. The <code>disable_drill_to_detail</code> field is a boolean specifying whether or not drill to detail is disabled for the database.<br>8. The <code>allow_multi_catalog</code> indicates if the database allows changing the default catalog when running queries and creating datasets.<br>9. The <code>disable_sampling_read_limit_override</code> field is a boolean specifying whether system-generated sampling queries (filter values, samples/preview, datetime format detection) that an engine rejects with a read-limit error should fail outright instead of being retried once with the engine's bounded-read override. Only affects engines that implement such an override.</p>|
|force_ctas_schema|string \| null|false|none|When allowing CREATE TABLE AS option in SQL Lab, this option forces the table to be created in this schema|
|id|integer|false|none|Database ID (for updates)|
|impersonate_user|boolean|false|none|If Presto, all the queries in SQL Lab are going to be executed as the currently logged on user who must have permission to run them.<br/>If Hive and hive.server2.enable.doAs is enabled, will run the queries as service account, but impersonate the currently logged on user via hive.server2.proxy.user property.|
|is_managed_externally|boolean \| null|false|none|none|
|masked_encrypted_extra|string \| null|false|none|<p>JSON string containing additional connection configuration.<br>This is used to provide connection information for systems like Hive, Presto, and BigQuery, which do not conform to the username:password syntax normally used by SQLAlchemy.</p>|
|parameters|object|false|none|DB-specific parameters for configuration|
|parameters_schema|object|false|none|JSONSchema for configuring the database by parameters instead of SQLAlchemy URI|
|server_cert|string \| null|false|none|<p>Optional CA_BUNDLE contents to validate HTTPS requests. Only available on certain database engines.</p>|
|sqlalchemy_uri|string|false|none|<p>Refer to the <a href="https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/rel_1_2/core/engines.html#database-urls" rel="noopener noreferrer">SqlAlchemy docs</a> for more information on how to structure your URI.</p>|
|ssh_tunnel|object \| null|false|none|none|
|uuid|string|false|none|none|

|configuration_method|string|true|none|Configuration_method is used on the frontend to inform the backend whether to explode parameters or to provide only a sqlalchemy_uri.|
|database_name|string \| null|false|none|A database name to identify this connection.|
|driver|string \| null|false|none|SQLAlchemy driver to use|
|engine|string|true|none|SQLAlchemy engine to use|
|extra|string|false|none|<p>JSON string containing extra configuration elements.<br>1. The <code>engine_params</code> object gets unpacked into the <a href="https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/core/engines.html#sqlalchemy.create_engine" rel="noopener noreferrer">sqlalchemy.create_engine</a> call, while the <code>metadata_params</code> gets unpacked into the <a href="https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/rel_1_0/core/metadata.html#sqlalchemy.schema.MetaData" rel="noopener noreferrer">sqlalchemy.MetaData</a> call.<br>2. The <code>metadata_cache_timeout</code> is a cache timeout setting in seconds for metadata fetch of this database. Specify it as <strong>"metadata_cache_timeout": {"schema_cache_timeout": 600, "table_cache_timeout": 600}</strong>. If unset, cache will not be enabled for the functionality. A timeout of 0 indicates that the cache never expires.<br>3. The <code>schemas_allowed_for_file_upload</code> is a comma separated list of schemas that CSVs are allowed to upload to. Specify it as <strong>"schemas_allowed_for_file_upload": ["public", "csv_upload"]</strong>. If database flavor does not support schema or any schema is allowed to be accessed, just leave the list empty<br>4. The <code>version</code> field is a string specifying the this db's version. This should be used with Presto DBs so that the syntax is correct<br>5. The <code>allows_virtual_table_explore</code> field is a boolean specifying whether or not the Explore button in SQL Lab results is shown.<br>6. The <code>disable_data_preview</code> field is a boolean specifying whether or not data preview queries will be run when fetching table metadata in SQL Lab.<br>7. The <code>disable_drill_to_detail</code> field is a boolean specifying whether or not drill to detail is disabled for the database.<br>8. The <code>allow_multi_catalog</code> indicates if the database allows changing the default catalog when running queries and creating datasets.<br>9. The <code>disable_sampling_read_limit_override</code> field is a boolean specifying whether system-generated sampling queries (filter values, samples/preview, datetime format detection) that an engine rejects with a read-limit error should fail outright instead of being retried once with the engine's bounded-read override. Only affects engines that implement such an override.</p>|
|id|integer \| null|false|none|Database ID (for updates)|
|impersonate_user|boolean|false|none|If Presto, all the queries in SQL Lab are going to be executed as the currently logged on user who must have permission to run them.<br/>If Hive and hive.server2.enable.doAs is enabled, will run the queries as service account, but impersonate the currently logged on user via hive.server2.proxy.user property.|
|masked_encrypted_extra|string \| null|false|none|<p>JSON string containing additional connection configuration.<br>This is used to provide connection information for systems like Hive, Presto, and BigQuery, which do not conform to the username:password syntax normally used by SQLAlchemy.</p>|
|parameters|object|false|none|DB-specific parameters for configuration|
|server_cert|string \| null|false|none|<p>Optional CA_BUNDLE contents to validate HTTPS requests. Only available on certain database engines.</p>|
|ssh_tunnel|object \| null|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_PartitionMappingPreviewSchema">PartitionMappingPreviewSchema</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->

<a id="schema_PartitionMappingPreviewSchema"></a>
<a id="tocSpartitionmappingpreviewschema"></a>
<a id="tocspartitionmappingpreviewschema"></a>

```json
{
  "is_monotonic": false,
  "mapped_column": "string",
  "operator": "==",
  "partition_column": null,
  "sample_values": [
    "string"
  ],
  "value_transform": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|is_monotonic|boolean|false|none|Whether the owner has declared the transform order-preserving. Range operators only mirror when they have.|
|mapped_column|string|true|none|Column whose filters would be mirrored|
|operator|string|false|none|Filter operator being mirrored. Only operators the preview can construct are accepted: TEMPORAL_RANGE is mirrored by the query path as two bounds decomposed from a since/until pair, which this request has no way to express.|
|partition_column|string \| null|false|none|Candidate partition column. The editor previews a mapping before it is saved, so this overrides the stored value; omitted, the stored one is used.|
|sample_values|[string]|true|none|Values to evaluate the transform at. A comparison operator takes one; IN takes the whole list.|
|value_transform|string \| null|true|none|SQL expression containing a :value placeholder|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|operator|<|
|operator|<=|
|operator|==|
|operator|>|
|operator|>=|
|operator|IN|

<h2 id="tocS_ReportConfigurationSchema">ReportConfigurationSchema</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemareportconfigurationschema"></a>
<a id="schema_ReportConfigurationSchema"></a>
<a id="tocSreportconfigurationschema"></a>
<a id="tocsreportconfigurationschema"></a>

```json
{
  "alert_minimum_interval": 3600,
  "alerts_attach_reports": true,
  "allowed_email_domains": [
    "example.com",
    "superset.com"
  ],
  "date_format_in_email_subject": true,
  "limit_recipients_to_users": true,
  "report_minimum_interval": 3600
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alert_minimum_interval|integer \| null|false|none|Minimum interval between alert executions, in seconds. Values below 120 do not restrict schedules. Falls back to ALERT_MINIMUM_INTERVAL only before this setting has been saved.|
|alerts_attach_reports|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether alerts deliver their attachment (screenshot, PDF, CSV or XLSX). When disabled, alerts only send the message and link. Falls back to the FF until a row has first been saved.|
|allowed_email_domains|[string]|false|none|E-mail domains accepted as recipients. An empty list allows any domain.|
|date_format_in_email_subject|boolean \| null|false|none|Render strftime date placeholders in email subjects. Falls back to the DATE_FORMAT_IN_EMAIL_SUBJECT FF until first saved.|
|limit_recipients_to_users|boolean \| null|false|none|When enabled, only e-mail addresses of existing active users are accepted as recipients.|
|report_minimum_interval|integer \| null|false|none|Minimum interval between report executions, in seconds. Values below 120 do not restrict schedules. Falls back to REPORT_MINIMUM_INTERVAL only before this setting has been saved.|

```json
{
```
```json
  "active": true,
```

```json
  "crontab": "*/5 * * * *",
  "custom_width": 1000,
  "dashboard": 0,
  "database": 0,
  "description": "Daily sales dashboard to marketing",
  "editors": [
    0
  ],
  "email_subject": "[Report]  Report name: Dashboard or chart name",
  "extra": {},
  "force_screenshot": true,
  "grace_period": 14400,
  "include_cta": true,
  "log_retention": 90,
  "name": "Daily dashboard email",
  "recipients": [
    {
      "recipient_config_json": {
        "bccTarget": "string",
        "ccTarget": "string",
        "target": "string"
      },
      "type": "Email"
    }
  ],
  "report_format": "PDF",
  "retry_max_attempts": 3,
  "retry_notify_owners": true,
  "retry_notify_recipients": false,
  "retry_on_failure": false,
  "run_alert_query_as": 0,
  "run_alert_query_as_type": "fixed_user",
  "run_as": 0,
  "run_as_type": "fixed_user",
  "send_failed_reports": false,
  "sql": "SELECT value FROM time_series_table",
  "timezone": "Africa/Abidjan",
  "type": "Alert",
  "validator_config_json": {
    "op": "<",
    "threshold": 0
  },
  "validator_type": "not null",
  "working_timeout": 3600
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean|false|none|none|
|chart|integer \| null|false|none|none|
|context_markdown|string \| null|false|none|Markdown description|
|creation_method|string|false|none|Creation method is used to inform the frontend whether the report/alert was created in the dashboard, chart, or alerts and reports UI.|
|crontab|string|true|none|A CRON expression.[Crontab Guru](https://crontab.guru/) is a helpful resource that can help you craft a CRON expression.|
|custom_width|integer \| null|false|none|Custom width of the screenshot in pixels|
|dashboard|integer \| null|false|none|none|
|database|integer|false|none|none|
|description|string \| null|false|none|Use a nice description to give context to this Alert/Report|
|editors|[integer \| object]|false|none|none|
|email_subject|string \| null|false|none|The report schedule subject line|
|extra|object|false|none|none|
|force_screenshot|boolean|false|none|none|
|grace_period|integer|false|none|Once an alert is triggered, how long, in seconds, before Superset nags you again. (in seconds)|
|include_cta|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether to include the call-to-action link back to Superset (e.g. 'Explore in Superset') in the delivered notifications|
|log_retention|integer|false|none|How long to keep the logs around for this report (in days)|
|name|string|true|none|The report schedule name.|
|recipients|[[ReportRecipient](#schemareportrecipient)]|false|none|none|
|report_format|string|false|none|Attachment format. NONE disables attachments for alerts and makes chart/dashboard optional. Omitted attachment settings are preserved on update.|
|retry_max_attempts|integer|false|none|Maximum number of retry attempts (1–10)|
|retry_notify_owners|boolean|false|none|Notify report owners on each retry attempt|
|retry_notify_recipients|boolean|false|none|Notify report recipients on each retry attempt|
|retry_on_failure|boolean|false|none|Enable automatic retries on report failure|
|run_alert_query_as|integer \| null|false|none|ID of the user whose credentials are used when running the alert condition SQL query, useful when the audience of the alert does not have access to the database. Null inherits the content executor at execution time.|
|run_alert_query_as_type|string \| null|false|none|Alert query executor type; null inherits run_as.|
|run_as|integer \| null|false|none|ID of the user whose credentials (RBAC permissions, database OAuth2 tokens) are used when rendering the content (screenshot, PDF, CSV, XLSX or text). Admins can set any active user; non-admins can only set themselves. Onlyhonored when the ALERT_REPORT_DYNAMIC_EXECUTOR feature flag is enabled. Admins can set this and run_as_type to null to use ALERT_REPORTS_EXECUTORS.|
|run_as_type|string \| null|false|none|Explicit executor type; fixed_user requires run_as.|
|send_failed_reports|boolean|false|none|Send the failed report to all recipients after retries are exhausted|
|sql|string|false|none|A SQL statement that defines whether the alert should get triggered or not. The query is expected to return either NULL or a number value.|
|timezone|string|false|none|A timezone string that represents the location of the timezone.|
|type|string|true|none|The report schedule type|
|validator_config_json|[ValidatorConfigJSON](#schemavalidatorconfigjson)|false|none|none|
|validator_type|string|false|none|Determines when to trigger alert based off value from alert query. Alerts will be triggered with these validator types:<br>- Not Null - When the return value is Not NULL, Empty, or 0<br>- Operator - When `sql_return_value comparison_operator threshold` is True e.g. `50 <= 75`<br>Supports the comparison operators <, <=, >, >=, ==, and !=|
|working_timeout|integer|false|none|If an alert is staled at a working state, how long until it's state is reset to error|

<a id="tocsreportschedulerestapi.put"></a>

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "chart": 0,
  "context_markdown": "string",
  "creation_method": "charts",
  "crontab": "string",
  "custom_width": 1000,
  "dashboard": 0,
  "database": 0,
  "description": "Daily sales dashboard to marketing",
  "editors": [
    0
  ],
  "email_subject": "[Report]  Report name: Dashboard or chart name",
  "extra": {},
  "force_screenshot": true,
  "grace_period": 14400,
  "include_cta": true,
  "log_retention": 90,
  "name": "string",
  "recipients": [
    {
      "recipient_config_json": {
        "bccTarget": "string",
        "ccTarget": "string",
        "target": "string"
      },
      "type": "Email"
    }
  ],
  "report_format": "PDF",
  "retry_max_attempts": 3,
  "retry_notify_owners": true,
  "retry_notify_recipients": true,
  "retry_on_failure": true,
  "run_alert_query_as": 0,
  "run_alert_query_as_type": "fixed_user",
  "run_as": 0,
  "run_as_type": "fixed_user",
  "send_failed_reports": true,
  "sql": "SELECT value FROM time_series_table",
  "timezone": "Africa/Abidjan",
  "type": "Alert",
  "validator_config_json": {
    "op": "<",
    "threshold": 0
  },
  "validator_type": "not null",
  "working_timeout": 3600
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|active|boolean|false|none|none|
|chart|integer \| null|false|none|none|
|context_markdown|string \| null|false|none|Markdown description|
|creation_method|string \| null|false|none|Creation method is used to inform the frontend whether the report/alert was created in the dashboard, chart, or alerts and reports UI.|
|crontab|string|false|none|A CRON expression.[Crontab Guru](https://crontab.guru/) is a helpful resource that can help you craft a CRON expression.|
|custom_width|integer \| null|false|none|Custom width of the screenshot in pixels|
|dashboard|integer \| null|false|none|none|
|database|integer \| null|false|none|none|
|description|string \| null|false|none|Use a nice description to give context to this Alert/Report|
|editors|[integer \| object]|false|none|none|
|email_subject|string \| null|false|none|The report schedule subject line|
|extra|object|false|none|none|
|force_screenshot|boolean|false|none|none|
|grace_period|integer|false|none|Once an alert is triggered, how long, in seconds, before Superset nags you again. (in seconds)|
|include_cta|boolean \| null|false|none|Whether to include the call-to-action link back to Superset (e.g. 'Explore in Superset') in the delivered notifications|
|log_retention|integer|false|none|How long to keep the logs around for this report (in days)|
|name|string|false|none|The report schedule name.|
|recipients|[[ReportRecipient](#schemareportrecipient)]|false|none|none|
|report_format|string|false|none|Attachment format. NONE disables attachments for alerts and makes chart/dashboard optional. Omitted attachment settings are preserved on update.|
|retry_max_attempts|integer|false|none|Maximum number of retry attempts (1–10)|
|retry_notify_owners|boolean|false|none|Notify report owners on each retry attempt|
|retry_notify_recipients|boolean|false|none|Notify report recipients on each retry attempt|
|retry_on_failure|boolean|false|none|Enable automatic retries on report failure|
|run_alert_query_as|integer \| null|false|none|ID of the user whose credentials are used when running the alert condition SQL query, useful when the audience of the alert does not have access to the database. Null inherits the content executor at execution time.|
|run_alert_query_as_type|string \| null|false|none|Alert query executor type; null inherits run_as.|
|run_as|integer \| null|false|none|ID of the user whose credentials (RBAC permissions, database OAuth2 tokens) are used when rendering the content (screenshot, PDF, CSV, XLSX or text). Admins can set any active user; non-admins can only set themselves. Onlyhonored when the ALERT_REPORT_DYNAMIC_EXECUTOR feature flag is enabled. Admins can set this and run_as_type to null to use ALERT_REPORTS_EXECUTORS.|
|run_as_type|string \| null|false|none|Explicit executor type; fixed_user requires run_as.|
|send_failed_reports|boolean|false|none|Send the failed report to all recipients after retries are exhausted|
|sql|string \| null|false|none|A SQL statement that defines whether the alert should get triggered or not. The query is expected to return either NULL or a number value.|
|timezone|string|false|none|A timezone string that represents the location of the timezone.|
|type|string|false|none|The report schedule type|
|validator_config_json|[ValidatorConfigJSON](#schemavalidatorconfigjson)|false|none|none|
|validator_type|string \| null|false|none|Determines when to trigger alert based off value from alert query. Alerts will be triggered with these validator types:<br>- Not Null - When the return value is Not NULL, Empty, or 0<br>- Operator - When `sql_return_value comparison_operator threshold` is True e.g. `50 <= 75`<br>Supports the comparison operators <, <=, >, >=, ==, and !=|
|working_timeout|integer \| null|false|none|If an alert is staled at a working state, how long until it's state is reset to error|

|decimal_character|string|false|none|[CSV and Excel only] Character to recognize as decimal point. Default is '.'|
|delimiter|string|false|none|[CSV only] The character used to separate values in the CSV file (e.g., a comma, semicolon, or tab).|
|file|string(text/csv)|true|none|The file to upload|
|header_row|integer|false|none|[CSV and Excel only] Row containing the headers to use as column names (0 is first line of data). Leave empty if there is no header row.|
|index_column|string|false|none|[CSV and Excel only] Column to use as the row labels of the dataframe. Leave empty if no index column|
|index_label|string|false|none|Index label for index column.|
|null_values|[string]|false|none|[CSV and Excel only] A list of strings that should be treated as null. Examples: '' for empty strings, 'None', 'N/A', Warning: Hive database supports only a single value|
|rows_to_read|integer \| null|false|none|[CSV and Excel only] Number of rows to read from the file. If None, reads all rows.|
|schema|string|false|none|The schema to upload the data file to.|
|sheet_name|string|false|none|[Excel only]] Strings used for sheet names (default is the first sheet).|
|skip_blank_lines|boolean|false|none|[CSV only] Skip blank lines in the CSV file.|
|skip_initial_space|boolean|false|none|[CSV only] Skip spaces after delimiter.|
|skip_rows|integer|false|none|[CSV and Excel only] Number of rows to skip at start of file.|
|table_name|string|true|none|The name of the table to be created/appended|
|type|string|true|none|File type to upload|

### Properties

|kind|string|false|none|Semantic category of the change. First-class values in V1: 'filter', 'metric', 'dimension', 'column', 'chart', 'time_range', 'color_palette'. Falls back to 'field' for generic scalar changes that don't map to a named kind.|
|operation|string|false|none|The verb for this change: 'add', 'remove', 'move', 'edit', 'update' (a collapsed-summary record for a field whose per-leaf changes exceeded the cap), or 'announce' (a synthetic headline record). Surfaced explicitly so consumers need not infer the verb from from_value/to_value null-tests — 'move' in particular cannot be derived that way.|
|path|object|false|none|Array of segments locating the change in the entity's state. Example: ['params', 'adhoc_filters', 'country'].|
|to_value|object \| null|false|none|Value at path after the save; null when the field was removed.|

```json
{
  "changed_by": {
    "first_name": "string",
    "id": 0,
    "last_name": "string"
  },
  "changes": [
    {
      "from_value": null,
      "kind": "string",
      "operation": "string",
      "path": null,
      "to_value": null
    }
  ],
  "issued_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "operation_type": "string",
  "transaction_id": 0,
  "version_number": 0,
  "version_uuid": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|changed_by|object \| null|false|none|User who produced the version, or null when the commit had no authenticated Flask user (CLI, Celery, import).|
|changes|[[VersionChangeRecord](#schemaversionchangerecord)]|false|none|Structured diff records describing the atomic field-level changes at this version, ordered by emission sequence. Empty for baseline (op=0) transactions per spec M4.|
|issued_at|string(date-time)|false|none|UTC timestamp of the commit that produced the row|
|operation_type|string|false|none|One of 'baseline', 'update', or 'delete', derived from the Continuum integer constant. Restore is not a distinct operation_type: a restore surfaces as 'update' carrying ``action_kind='restore'`` (see ACTIVITY_ACTION_KINDS).|
|transaction_id|integer|false|none|Underlying Continuum transaction id|
|version_number|integer|false|none|0-based position in the history, oldest first|
|version_uuid|string(uuid)|false|none|Deterministic UUIDv5 derived from the entity UUID and the Continuum transaction id — stable across replicas and retention pruning. The handle accepted by the get/restore version endpoints.|
